    @property

class ICmdLineOption:
    """Base class for command line options."""
    @property
    def names(self) -> list[str]:
        """Get the names."""

    @property
    def hasValue(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the option takes a value."""

    @property
    def help(self) -> str:
        """Get the help: the names, whether a value follows, and the text."""

    @property
    def helpText(self) -> str:
        """Get the help text alone, without the names."""

    @property
    def group(self) -> str:
        """Get the group."""

    @property
    def found(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the option was found."""

    @property
    def matchedName(self) -> str:
        """Get the option name that was matched."""

class CmdLineFlag(ICmdLineOption):
    """Command line flag."""
    def __init__(self, names: Sequence[str], help: str, group: str = '') -> None: ...

class CmdLineOptionI(ICmdLineOption):
    def __init__(self, names: Sequence[str], help: str, group: str = '', defaultValue: int | None = None, possibleValues: str = '') -> None: ...

    @property
    def hasValue(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> int: ...

class CmdLineOptionF(ICmdLineOption):
    def __init__(self, names: Sequence[str], help: str, group: str = '', defaultValue: float | None = None, possibleValues: str = '') -> None: ...

    @property
    def hasValue(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> float: ...

class CmdLineOptionD(ICmdLineOption):
    def __init__(self, names: Sequence[str], help: str, group: str = '', defaultValue: float | None = None, possibleValues: str = '') -> None: ...

    @property
    def hasValue(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> float: ...

class CmdLineOptionBool(ICmdLineOption):
    def __init__(self, names: Sequence[str], help: str, group: str = '', defaultValue: bool | None = None, possibleValues: str = '') -> None: ...

    @property
    def hasValue(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> bool: ...

class CmdLineOptionString(ICmdLineOption):
    def __init__(self, names: Sequence[str], help: str, group: str = '', defaultValue: str | None = None, possibleValues: str = '') -> None: ...

    @property
    def hasValue(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> str: ...

class CmdLineListOptionString(ICmdLineOption):
    def __init__(self, names: Sequence[str], help: str, group: str = '') -> None: ...

    @property
    def list(self) -> list[str]: ...

class ICmdLineArg:
    """Base class for command line arguments."""
    pass

class CmdLineArgI(ICmdLineArg):
    def __init__(self, name: str, help: str, optional: bool = False) -> None: ...

    @property
    def hasValue(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> int: ...

class CmdLineArgF(ICmdLineArg):
    def __init__(self, name: str, help: str, optional: bool = False) -> None: ...

    @property
    def hasValue(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> float: ...

class CmdLineArgD(ICmdLineArg):
    def __init__(self, name: str, help: str, optional: bool = False) -> None: ...

    @property
    def hasValue(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> float: ...

class CmdLineArgBool(ICmdLineArg):
    def __init__(self, name: str, help: str, optional: bool = False) -> None: ...

    @property
    def hasValue(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> bool: ...

class CmdLineArgString(ICmdLineArg):
    def __init__(self, name: str, help: str, optional: bool = False) -> None: ...

    @property
    def hasValue(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> str: ...

class CmdLineListArgString(ICmdLineArg):
    def __init__(self, name: str, help: str, optional: bool = False) -> None: ...

    @property
    def list(self) -> list[str]: ...

class Color1F:
    """One channel color (luminance)."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def __setitem__(self, arg0: int, arg1: float, /) -> None: ...

    def __getitem__(self, arg: int, /) -> float: ...

    @property
    def l(self) -> float:
        """The luminance."""

    @l.setter
    def l(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: Color1F, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: Color1F, /) -> bool: ...

    def __repr__(self) -> str: ...

class Color2F:

    @overload

    def __setitem__(self, arg0: int, arg1: float, /) -> None: ...

    def __getitem__(self, arg: int, /) -> float: ...

    @property
    def l(self) -> float:
        """The luminance."""

    @l.setter
    def l(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def a(self) -> float:
        """The alpha."""

    @a.setter
    def a(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: Color2F, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: Color2F, /) -> bool: ...

    def __repr__(self) -> str: ...

class ICommand:
    """Base class for commands."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    def exec(self) -> None:
        """Execute the command. A command stack calls this when the command is
        pushed, and again when it is redone.
        """

    def undo(self) -> None:
        """Undo the command."""

class CommandStack:
    """Command stack."""
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Create a new command stack."""

    def push(self, command: ICommand) -> None:
        """Execute a command and push it onto the stack."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear the stack."""

    def undo(self) -> None:
        """Undo a command."""

    def redo(self) -> None:
        """Redo a command."""

    def observeHasUndo(self) -> IObservableBool:
        """Observer whether the stack can undo a command."""

    def observeHasRedo(self) -> IObservableBool:
        """Observer whether the stack can redo a command."""

class Context:
    """
    The systems an application runs on: logging, fonts, I/O, audio and whatever else is added. Everything made from a context is updated by tick().
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Create a new context."""

    def addSystem(self, arg: IBaseSystem, /) -> None:
        """Add a system."""

    @property
    def systems(self) -> list[IBaseSystem]:
        """Get the systems."""

    def getSystemByName(self, arg: str, /) -> IBaseSystem:
        """Get a system by name."""

    def tick(self) -> None:
        """
        Run the systems once: results from other threads are taken in, a player's current frame and time move on, and observers are called. Nothing changes between calls, so a script without an application's event loop calls this in its own loop, for as long as it is waiting for something. It does not wait itself: it takes in only what has finished, so sleep a few milliseconds between calls. A loop of bare calls can run a thousand times before the first frame is decoded.
        """

class DiagFormat:
    """How a sample is turned into the number its format string expects.

    Samples are integers, which is right for counting things and wrong for
    timing them: the resolution wanted for a graph and the unit wanted for
    reading are not the same. Sample in microseconds, divide by a thousand and
    show one decimal, and the graph keeps its detail while the label says
    milliseconds.
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def divisor(self) -> float:
        """What a sample is divided by before it is formatted. It is only used
        when the precision is zero or more.
        """

    @divisor.setter
    def divisor(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def precision(self) -> int:
        """Decimal places. Below zero formats the sample as the integer it is.
        """

    @precision.setter
    def precision(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

def diagText(format: str, diagFormat: DiagFormat, value: int) -> str:
    """Apply a sampler's format to a sample."""

class DiagSystem(ISystem):
    """Diagnostics system."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context) -> None:
        """Create a new system."""

    def addSampler(self, id: str, sampler: Callable[[], int], format: DiagFormat = ...) -> None:
        """Add a sampler function. The id is the group and then the name,
        "Group/Name: {0}", the name being the format string for the readout. An
        id already added is left as it is.
        """

    def getFormat(self, id: str) -> DiagFormat:
        """Get how a sampler's value should be formatted."""

    @property
    def groups(self) -> list[str]:
        """The sampler groups, in the order they are shown."""

    @property
    def groupOrder(self) -> list[str]:
        """
        The groups shown first, in order; the rest follow in the order they were added.
        """

    @groupOrder.setter
    def groupOrder(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    def getNames(self, group: str) -> list[str]:
        """Get the sampler names in a group."""

    def hasSampler(self, id: str) -> bool:
        """Get whether the sampler exists."""

    @property
    def samplesMax(self) -> int:
        """Get the maximum number of samples."""

    @samplesMax.setter
    def samplesMax(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    def observeSamplesMax(self) -> IObservableSizeT:
        """Observe the maximum number of samples."""

    @property
    def samples(self) -> dict[str, list[int]]:
        """Get the samples."""

    @property
    def tickTime(self) -> datetime.timedelta:
        """Get the system tick time interval."""

    @tickTime.setter
    def tickTime(self, arg: datetime.timedelta, /) -> None: ...

class FileLogSystem(ISystem):
    """File logging system."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, path: str | os.PathLike) -> None:
        """Create a new system."""

class FontInfo:
    """Font information."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg0: str, arg1: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """The font name: a built-in font (see getDefaultFont()) or one added
        to the font system. A name the font system does not have is drawn with
        the default regular font.
        """

    @name.setter
    def name(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def size(self) -> int:
        """The font size, in pixels."""

    @size.setter
    def size(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: FontInfo, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: FontInfo, /) -> bool: ...

    def __lt__(self, arg: FontInfo, /) -> bool: ...

class FontMetrics:
    """Font metrics."""
    @property
    def ascender(self) -> int:
        """The distance from the baseline up to the top of the font, in pixels.
        """

    @ascender.setter
    def ascender(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def descender(self) -> int:
        """The distance from the baseline to the bottom of the font, in pixels.
        It is below the baseline, so it is usually negative.
        """

    @descender.setter
    def descender(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def lineHeight(self) -> int:
        """The distance from one baseline to the next, in pixels."""

    @lineHeight.setter
    def lineHeight(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

class GlyphInfo:
    """Font glyph information."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg0: int, arg1: FontInfo, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def code(self) -> int:
        """The Unicode code point."""

    @code.setter
    def code(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def fontInfo(self) -> FontInfo:
        """The font."""

    @fontInfo.setter
    def fontInfo(self, arg: FontInfo, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: GlyphInfo, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: GlyphInfo, /) -> bool: ...

    def __lt__(self, arg: GlyphInfo, /) -> bool: ...

class Glyph:
    """Font glyph."""
    @property
    def info(self) -> GlyphInfo:
        """The code point and font the glyph is for."""

    @info.setter
    def info(self, arg: GlyphInfo, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def image(self) -> Image:
        """The rendered glyph: one channel of 8-bit coverage. Null when no font
        has the glyph or it cannot be rendered.
        """

    @image.setter
    def image(self, arg: Image, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def offset(self) -> V2I:
        """Where the top left of the image is from the pen position on the
        baseline, in pixels, with y up.
        """

    @offset.setter
    def offset(self, arg: V2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def advance(self) -> int:
        """How far the pen moves on to the next glyph, in pixels."""

    @advance.setter
    def advance(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def lsbDelta(self) -> int:
        """The change hinting made to the left side bearing, in 64ths of a
        pixel. Text layout compares it with the previous glyph's rsbDelta and
        moves the glyph a pixel when they differ by more than about half a
        pixel.
        """

    @lsbDelta.setter
    def lsbDelta(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def rsbDelta(self) -> int:
        """The change hinting made to the right side bearing, in 64ths of a
        pixel.
        """

    @rsbDelta.setter
    def rsbDelta(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

class FontSystem(ISystem):
    """Font system.

    Add text elide functionality. Add support for gamma correction?
    - https://www.freetype.org/freetype2/docs/text-rendering-general.html
    Use a text-shaping library.
    """
    def __init__(self, context: Context) -> None:
        """Create a new system."""

    @property
    def fonts(self) -> list[str]:
        """Get the names of the fonts."""

    def addFont(self, name: str, fileName: str) -> bool:
        """Add a font from a file, under the given name.

        Add a font from data in memory, which is copied, under the given name.
        Returns whether the font could be read.
        """

    @property
    def glyphCacheSize(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of glyphs in the cache. It is updated once a second.
        """

    def observeGlyphCacheSize(self) -> IObservableSizeT:
        """Observe the number of glyphs in the cache."""

    @property
    def glyphCachePercentage(self) -> float:
        """Get how full the glyph cache is, as a percentage of its maximum. It
        is updated once a second.
        """

    def getMetrics(self, fontInfo: FontInfo) -> FontMetrics:
        """Get font metrics."""

    def getSize(self, text: str, fontInfo: FontInfo, maxLineWidth: int = 0) -> Size2I:
        """Get the size of the given string."""

    def getBoxes(self, text: str, fontInfo: FontInfo, maxLineWidth: int = 0) -> list[Box2I]:
        """Get the character boxes for the given string."""

    def getGlyphs(self, text: str, fontInfo: FontInfo) -> list[Glyph]:
        """Get the glyphs for the given string."""

        """Draw text."""

        """Draw text."""

class ImageType(enum.Enum):
    """Image types."""
    L_U8 = 1

    L_U16 = 2

    L_U32 = 3

    L_F16 = 4

    L_F32 = 5

    LA_U8 = 6

    LA_U16 = 7

    LA_U32 = 8

    LA_F16 = 9

    LA_F32 = 10

    RGB_U8 = 11

    RGB_U10 = 12

    RGB_U16 = 13

    RGB_U32 = 14

    RGB_F16 = 15

    RGB_F32 = 16

    RGBA_U8 = 17

    RGBA_U16 = 18

    RGBA_U32 = 19

    RGBA_F16 = 20

    RGBA_F32 = 21

    YUV_420P_U8 = 22

    YUV_422P_U8 = 23

    YUV_444P_U8 = 24

    YUV_420P_U16 = 25

    YUV_422P_U16 = 26

    YUV_444P_U16 = 27

    YUV_420SP_U8 = 28
    """Semi-planar 4:2:0 8-bit (e.g. hardware-decoded NV12)"""

    YUV_420SP_U16 = 29
    """Semi-planar 4:2:0 16-bit (e.g. hardware-decoded P010)"""

    RGB_F16_P = 30
    """Planar three channel half float: red, then green, then blue, each its
    own plane.

    The same bytes as RGB_F16 in a different order, uploaded as three single
    channel textures rather than one three channel one. There is no three
    channel half format on Metal, so a RGB_F16 texture is backed by a four
    channel one and every upload of it is widened by the driver; three single
    channel textures are each a format that does exist, so nothing is widened.

    Added at the end deliberately: the shaders carry these values as literals,
    so inserting one anywhere else renumbers them.
    """

def getImageTypeEnums() -> list[ImageType]:
    """Get every value of ImageType."""

        """Get the number of observers."""

        """Set the value."""

        """Set the value only if it has changed."""

    def get(self) -> ImageType:
        """Get the value."""

class ImageMirror:
    """Image mirroring."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg0: bool, arg1: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def x(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the image is mirrored horizontally: each row is stored right
        to left.
        """

    @x.setter
    def x(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def y(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the image is mirrored vertically: the rows are stored top
        down. By default they are stored bottom up, the first row in memory
        being the bottom of the image.
        """

    @y.setter
    def y(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: ImageMirror, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: ImageMirror, /) -> bool: ...

class ImageLayout:
    """Image data layout."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg0: ImageMirror, arg1: int, arg2: Endian, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def mirror(self) -> ImageMirror:
        """How the data is mirrored."""

    @mirror.setter
    def mirror(self, arg: ImageMirror, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def alignment(self) -> int:
        """The row alignment, in bytes: each row of data is padded to a
        multiple of it. The planar YUV types are not padded.
        """

    @alignment.setter
    def alignment(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def endian(self) -> Endian:
        """The byte order of samples larger than a byte. The default is the
        machine's own.
        """

    @endian.setter
    def endian(self, arg: Endian, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: ImageLayout, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: ImageLayout, /) -> bool: ...

class ImageInfo:
    """Image information."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg0: Size2I, arg1: ImageType, /) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg0: int, arg1: int, arg2: ImageType, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """The image name, such as the name of the layer it was read from."""

    @name.setter
    def name(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def size(self) -> Size2I:
        """The size, in pixels."""

    @size.setter
    def size(self, arg: Size2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def type(self) -> ImageType:
        """The pixel type. The information is not valid while it is None."""

    @type.setter
    def type(self, arg: ImageType, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def pixelAspectRatio(self) -> float:
        """The pixel aspect ratio: the width of a pixel over its height."""

    @pixelAspectRatio.setter
    def pixelAspectRatio(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def videoLevels(self) -> VideoLevels:
        """The range the samples use. The renderers expand legal range to full,
        unless ImageOptions::videoLevels says otherwise.
        """

    @videoLevels.setter
    def videoLevels(self, arg: VideoLevels, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def yuvCoefficients(self) -> YUVCoefficients:
        """The coefficients the YUV types are converted to RGB with."""

    @yuvCoefficients.setter
    def yuvCoefficients(self, arg: YUVCoefficients, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def depth(self) -> int:
        """The bits in each sample when fewer than the type holds: 10 or 12-bit
        video kept in 16-bit words with its value in the low bits, as decoders
        hand it over. Zero is the type's own depth. The renderers scale such
        samples up; see getSampleScale().
        """

    @depth.setter
    def depth(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def layout(self) -> ImageLayout:
        """The data layout: mirroring, row alignment, and byte order."""

    @layout.setter
    def layout(self, arg: ImageLayout, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def valid(self) -> bool:
        """Is the information valid?"""

    @property
    def aspect(self) -> float:
        """Get the aspect ratio."""

    @property
    def byteCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of bytes used to store an image."""

    def __eq__(self, arg: ImageInfo, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: ImageInfo, /) -> bool: ...

class Image:
    """Image."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg: ImageInfo, /) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg0: Size2I, arg1: ImageType, /) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg0: int, arg1: int, arg2: ImageType, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def info(self) -> ImageInfo:
        """Get the image information."""

    @property
    def size(self) -> Size2I:
        """Get the image size."""

    @property
    def width(self) -> int:
        """Get the image width."""

    @property
    def height(self) -> int:
        """Get the image height."""

    @property
    def aspect(self) -> float:
        """Get the aspect ratio."""

    @property
    def type(self) -> ImageType:
        """Get the image type."""

    @property
    def valid(self) -> bool:
        """Is the image valid?"""

    @property
    def tags(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Get the image tags."""

    @tags.setter
    def tags(self, arg: Mapping[str, str], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def byteCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of bytes used to store the image data."""

    def zero(self) -> None:
        """Zero the image data."""

    @property
    def data(self) -> memoryview:
        """
        The pixels as a memoryview of (height, width, channels) over the image's own memory, row zero at the top whatever the layout's mirror. Writing to it writes the image.
        """

    def __array__(self, dtype: object | None = None, copy: object | None = None) -> object: ...

class LogType(enum.Enum):
    """Log types."""
    Message = 0

    Warning = 1

    Error = 2

def getLogTypeEnums() -> list[LogType]:
    """Get every value of LogType."""

class LogItem:
    """Log item."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def time(self) -> datetime.datetime:
        """When the item was logged. Wall clock rather than time since the
        application started: a log is read after the fact, and lining an entry
        up with when something happened is the whole point of it.
        """

    @time.setter
    def time(self, arg: datetime.datetime | datetime.date | datetime.time, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def prefix(self) -> str:
        """What logged the item, such as "ftk::FontSystem"."""

    @prefix.setter
    def prefix(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def message(self) -> str:
        """The message."""

    @message.setter
    def message(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def type(self) -> LogType:
        """Whether the item is a message, a warning, or an error."""

    @type.setter
    def type(self, arg: LogType, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: LogItem, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: LogItem, /) -> bool: ...

class LogItemListObserver:
    """List observer."""
    def __init__(self, observableList: IObservableLogItemList, callback: Callable[[Sequence[LogItem]], None], action: ObserverAction = ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

class IObservableLogItemList:
    """Base class for observable lists."""
    pass

class ObservableLogItemList(IObservableLogItemList):
    """Observable list."""
    def __init__(self, arg: Sequence[LogItem], /) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, arg: Sequence[LogItem], /) -> None:
        """Set the list."""

    def setIfChanged(self, arg: Sequence[LogItem], /) -> bool:
        """Set the list only if it has changed."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear the list."""

    def setItem(self, index: int, value: LogItem) -> None:
        """Set an item."""

    def setItemOnlyIfChanged(self, index: int, value: LogItem) -> bool:
        """Set an item only if it has changed."""

    @overload
    def pushBack(self, arg: LogItem, /) -> None:
        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

    @overload
    def pushBack(self, arg: Sequence[LogItem], /) -> None:
        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

    def insertItem(self, index: int, value: LogItem) -> None:
        """Insert an item."""

    def insertItems(self, index: int, list: Sequence[LogItem]) -> None:
        """Insert a range of items."""

    def removeItem(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Remove an item."""

    def removeItems(self, start: int, end: int) -> None:
        """Remove a range of items."""

    def replaceItems(self, start: int, end: int, list: Sequence[LogItem]) -> None:
        """Replace a range of items."""

    def get(self) -> list[LogItem]:
        """Get the list."""

    def getSize(self) -> int:
        """Get the list size."""

    def isEmpty(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the list is empty."""

    def getItem(self, arg: int, /) -> LogItem:
        """Get a list item."""

    def contains(self, arg: LogItem, /) -> bool:
        """Does the list contain the given item?"""

    def indexOf(self, arg: LogItem, /) -> int:
        """Get the index of the given item."""

    """Create a translation matrix."""

    """Create a translation matrix."""

    """Create a X rotation matrix."""

    """Create a Y rotation matrix."""

    """Create a Z rotation matrix."""

def rotate(arg0: float, arg1: V3F, /) -> M44F:
    """Create a rotation matrix about an arbitrary axis.

    The axis is normalized; a zero-length one gives the identity.
    """

def rotateXYZ(arg: V3F, /) -> M44F:
    """Create a rotation matrix from angles about the X, Y and Z axes, applied
    in that order.
    """

def getRotateXYZ(arg0: M44F, arg1: V3F, /) -> V3F:
    """Get angles rotateXYZ() builds the given rotation from.

    Two sets of angles describe any rotation, and each of those has more
    versions of itself whole turns apart, so which one to return cannot be
    derived -- it has to be asked for. The one returned is whichever is nearest
    nearAngles.

    A manipulator dragging a rotation passes the angles its last move wrote.
    That is what keeps a gesture round and round winding past a full turn
    rather than starting again at zero, and what stops a drag crossing the pose
    where the Y angle folds back from taking the long way round to describe it.
    Somewhere with no previous answer to be near -- reading a matrix that
    arrived from elsewhere -- can pass zero.

    Straight up or straight down the Y axis, the X and Z rotations are about
    the same axis and only their sum is decided; it is given to Z.
    """

def scale(arg: V3F, /) -> M44F:
    """Create a scale matrix."""

def ortho(arg0: float, arg1: float, arg2: float, arg3: float, arg4: float, arg5: float, /) -> M44F:
    """Create an orthographic matrix."""

def perspective(arg0: float, arg1: float, arg2: float, arg3: float, /) -> M44F:
    """Create a perspective matrix."""

def invert(arg0: M44F, arg1: M44F, /) -> bool:
    """Invert a matrix."""

class Noise:
    """Noise

    References:
    - https://mrl.cs.nyu.edu/~perlin/noise/
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    def get(self, x: float, y: float, z: float) -> float:
        """Get the noise at a point, roughly between -1 and 1. It is zero where
        x, y and z are all whole numbers, and repeats every 256 units on each
        axis. Every Noise gives the same values.
        """

class UserPath(enum.Enum):
    """User paths."""
    Home = 0

    Desktop = 1

    Documents = 2

    Downloads = 3

    Config = 4
    """Where an application keeps its own files -- settings, logs, recovery
    state: "Application Support" on macOS, the roaming AppData directory on
    Windows, XDG_CONFIG_HOME or ~/.config elsewhere. Not Documents, which cloud
    drives sync and macOS gates behind a permission prompt; a log rewritten on
    every launch trips over both.
    """

def getUserPathEnums() -> list[UserPath]:
    """Get every value of UserPath."""

def getUserPath(arg: UserPath, /) -> str:
    """Get a user path."""

    """File path options."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: PathOptions, /) -> bool: ...

class FrameSeq:
    """Frame sequence."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, range: RangeI64, inc: int = 1) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, min: int, max: int, inc: int = 1) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, frame: int) -> None: ...

    @property
    def range(self) -> RangeI64:
        """The first and last frames."""

    @range.setter
    def range(self, arg: RangeI64, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def inc(self) -> int:
        """The step between frames: 1 for every frame, 2 for every other one.
        """

    @inc.setter
    def inc(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: FrameSeq, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: FrameSeq, /) -> bool: ...

def toFrameSeq(frames: Sequence[int]) -> list[FrameSeq]:
    """Convert frames to frame sequences."""

def toFrames(seq: Sequence[FrameSeq]) -> list[int]:
    """Convert a frame sequence to frames.

    Convert frame sequences to frames.
    """

def addFrame(seq: Sequence[FrameSeq], frame: int) -> list[FrameSeq]:
    """Add a frame to a list of frame sequences, which is kept sorted and
    merged. Frames already in the list are ignored.

    Adding frames in order gives the same result as toFrameSeq(); frames added
    out of order may be split into a different set of sequences that covers the
    same frames.
    """

def getFrameCount(seq: Sequence[FrameSeq]) -> int:
    """Get the number of frames in a frame sequence.

    Get the number of frames in a list of frame sequences.
    """

def getRange(seq: Sequence[FrameSeq]) -> RangeI64 | None:
    """Get the range the value is kept within."""

def getStep(seq: Sequence[FrameSeq]) -> int:
    """Get the step: how much the up and down arrow keys, the increment
    buttons, and the scroll wheel change the value by.
    """

def getMissingCount(seq: Sequence[FrameSeq]) -> int:
    """Get how many frames are missing from a list of frame sequences: the
    frames at its step, between its first and last, that it does not have.
    Frames 1, 3, 7 and 9 are missing one, frame 5.
    """

def getMissing(seq: Sequence[FrameSeq]) -> list[FrameSeq]:
    """Get the frames missing from a list of frame sequences, as
    getMissingCount() counts them: for frames 1, 3, 7 and 9, frame 5.
    """

class Path:
    """File path.

    Example: file:///tmp/render.0001.exr?user=foo;password=bar
    * protocol: file://
    * dir: /tmp/
    * base: render.
    * number: 0001
    * padding: 4
    * extension: .exr
    * request: ?user=foo;password=bar
    * file name: render.0001.exr
    """
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg0: str, arg1: str, /) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg0: str, arg1: PathOptions, /) -> None: ...

    def get(self) -> str:
        """Get the path as a string."""

    @property
    def isEmpty(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the path is empty."""

    @property
    def hasProtocol(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the path has a protocol."""

    @property
    def hasSeqWildcard(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether this has a sequence wildcard ('#')."""

    @property
    def hasDir(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the path has a directory."""

    @property
    def hasBase(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the path has a base name."""

    @property
    def hasNum(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the path has a frame number, or a "#" wildcard."""

    @property
    def hasExt(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the path has an extension."""

    @property
    def hasRequest(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the path has a request."""

    @property
    def protocol(self) -> str:
        """Get the protocol, such as "file://"."""

    @protocol.setter
    def protocol(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def dir(self) -> str:
        """Get the directory, with its trailing separator, such as "/tmp/"."""

    @dir.setter
    def dir(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def base(self) -> str:
        """Get the base name: what comes before the frame number and the
        extension, such as "render.".
        """

    @base.setter
    def base(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def num(self) -> str:
        """Get the frame number as it is written, such as "0001", or the "#"
        wildcard.
        """

    @num.setter
    def num(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def pad(self) -> int:
        """Get the frame number padding: the number of digits when the number
        starts with a zero or is a wildcard, and zero otherwise.
        """

    @pad.setter
    def pad(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def ext(self) -> str:
        """Get the extension, with its dot, such as ".exr"."""

    @ext.setter
    def ext(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def request(self) -> str:
        """Get the request, with its question mark, such as "?user=foo"."""

    @request.setter
    def request(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def fileName(self) -> str:
        """Get the file name: the base name, frame number and extension, after
        the directory when dir is true. The protocol and the request are left
        out.
        """

    @fileName.setter
    def fileName(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    def getFileName(self, dir: bool = False) -> str:
        """Get the file name: the base name, frame number and extension, after
        the directory when dir is true. The protocol and the request are left
        out.
        """

    @property
    def frames(self) -> RangeI64 | None:
        """Get the range spanned by the sequence. This is the range from the
        first to the last frame, which for a partial sequence includes frames
        that are missing; use getSeq() for the frames themselves.
        """

    @frames.setter
    def frames(self, arg: RangeI64, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def frameSeq(self) -> list[FrameSeq]:
        """Get the frames in the sequence."""

    @frameSeq.setter
    def frameSeq(self, arg: Sequence[FrameSeq], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def seqSize(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of frames in the sequence."""

    @property
    def isSeq(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether this is a sequence."""

    @property
    def isPartialSeq(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether this sequence is missing frames within its range."""

    def getFrame(self, frame: int, dir: bool = False) -> str:
        """Get a file name with the given frame number."""

    def getFrameRange(self, count: bool = False) -> str:
        """Get the frame range string. When count is true a sequence that is
        missing frames says how many, e.g. "0001-0020 (8 missing)", and one on
        a step with none missing says the step, e.g. "0001-0019 (step 2)" --
        what a file browser shows, so that a broken render is seen before it is
        opened.
        """

    def seq(self, path: Path) -> bool:
        """Get whether a path is part of this sequence."""

    def addSeq(self, path: Path) -> bool:
        """Add a path to this sequence."""

    @property
    def isAbs(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the path is absolute."""

    def testExt(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> bool:
        """Test whether this extension matches one in the given list."""

    def getNumbers() -> str:
        """Get the characters a frame number is made of: the digits and "#"."""

    def getPathSeparators() -> str:
        """Get the characters that separate directories: forward slash and
        backslash.
        """

    def __eq__(self, arg: Path, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: Path, /) -> bool: ...

class DirListSort(enum.Enum):
    """Directory list sorting."""
    Name = 0

    Extension = 1

    Size = 2

    Time = 3

def getDirListSortEnums() -> list[DirListSort]:
    """Get every value of DirListSort."""

class DirListOptions:
    """Directory list options."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def sort(self) -> DirListSort:
        """How the entries are sorted. Directories come first whatever the
        sort.
        """

    @sort.setter
    def sort(self, arg: DirListSort, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def sortReverse(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the sort is reversed."""

    @sortReverse.setter
    def sortReverse(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def filter(self) -> str:
        """Case-insensitive match against the file name: a substring, or a
        wildcard pattern when it contains "*" or "?". A directory that is
        entered is exempt from the filter -- it is the route to the files, not
        what is being looked for -- while one at the last level is subject to
        it like anything else.
        """

    @filter.setter
    def filter(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def filterFiles(self) -> bool:
        """Whether to leave the files out, listing only directories."""

    @filterFiles.setter
    def filterFiles(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def filterExt(self) -> list[str]:
        """The extensions of the files to list, lower case with the dot, such
        as ".exr". Empty lists every file. Directories are not filtered.
        """

    @filterExt.setter
    def filterExt(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def seq(self) -> bool:
        """Whether numbered files are grouped into sequences, each listed as
        one entry.
        """

    @seq.setter
    def seq(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def seqExts(self) -> list[str]:
        """The extensions of the files that are grouped into sequences, lower
        case with the dot. Empty groups any file.
        """

    @seqExts.setter
    def seqExts(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def seqNegative(self) -> bool:
        """Whether a minus in front of a frame number makes it negative; see
        PathOptions::seqNegative.
        """

    @seqNegative.setter
    def seqNegative(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def seqMaxDigits(self) -> int:
        """The most digits a frame number can have; see
        PathOptions::seqMaxDigits.
        """

    @seqMaxDigits.setter
    def seqMaxDigits(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def hidden(self) -> bool:
        """Whether to list the files and directories whose names start with a
        dot.
        """

    @hidden.setter
    def hidden(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def depth(self) -> int:
        """How many directory levels to list: 1 is the directory alone. Deeper
        levels follow their directory's entry, each listed with these same
        options, so the order is deterministic. Directory links are listed but
        never entered, which also keeps a cycle of links from listing forever.
        """

    @depth.setter
    def depth(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: DirListOptions, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: DirListOptions, /) -> bool: ...

class DirEntry:
    """Directory list entry."""
    @property
    def path(self) -> Path:
        """The path. For a sequence it names the first frame and holds the
        frames found.
        """

    @path.setter
    def path(self, arg: Path, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def isDir(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the entry is a directory."""

    @isDir.setter
    def isDir(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def size(self) -> int:
        """The size, in bytes: for a sequence the total of its files, and zero
        for a directory.
        """

    @size.setter
    def size(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def time(self) -> datetime.datetime:
        """When the entry was last written. For a sequence, the latest of its
        files.
        """

    @time.setter
    def time(self, arg: datetime.datetime | datetime.date | datetime.time, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: DirEntry, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: DirEntry, /) -> bool: ...

def dirList(path: str, options: DirListOptions = ...) -> list[DirEntry]:
    """How the directory is listed: the sort order, sequences and hidden files.
    """

def expandSeq(path: Path, pathOptions: PathOptions = ...) -> Path:
    """Expand a file sequence. This function will search the directory for
    other frames that match the given file name.
    """

class Random:
    """Random numbers."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def getF(self) -> float:
        """Get a random number between zero and one.

        Get a random number between zero and the given value.

        Get a random number between two values.
        """

    @overload
    def getF(self, arg: float, /) -> float:
        """Get a random number between zero and one.

        Get a random number between zero and the given value.

        Get a random number between two values.
        """

    @overload
    def getF(self, min: float, max: float) -> float:
        """Get a random number between zero and one.

        Get a random number between zero and the given value.

        Get a random number between two values.
        """

    @overload
    def getI(self, arg: int, /) -> int:
        """Get a random number between zero and the given value.

        Get a random number between two values.
        """

    @overload
    def getI(self, min: int, max: int) -> int:
        """Get a random number between zero and the given value.

        Get a random number between two values.
        """

    @overload
    def setSeed(self, arg: int, /) -> None:
        """Seed the random value generator.

        Seed the random value generator with the current time.
        """

    @overload
    def setSeed(self) -> None:
        """Seed the random value generator.

        Seed the random value generator with the current time.
        """

class RenderOptions:
    """Render options."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def clear(self) -> bool:
        """Clear the canvas before rendering."""

    @clear.setter
    def clear(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def clearColor(self) -> Color4F:
        """Clear color."""

    @clearColor.setter
    def clearColor(self, arg: Color4F, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def texturePoolByteCount(self) -> int:
        """Texture pool byte count (enough for two 4K RGBA 16-bit frames). The
        GPU renderer counts an entry with its transfer buffers and holds the
        pool to this at the end of each frame, by the entries that frame did
        not draw with.
        """

    @texturePoolByteCount.setter
    def texturePoolByteCount(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def textureCacheByteCount(self) -> int:
        """Texture cache byte count."""

    @textureCacheByteCount.setter
    def textureCacheByteCount(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def glyphAtlasSize(self) -> int:
        """Glyph texture atlas size. Zero is the renderer's own choice: smaller
        where the graphics API is the more constrained one.
        """

    @glyphAtlasSize.setter
    def glyphAtlasSize(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def log(self) -> bool:
        """Enable logging."""

    @log.setter
    def log(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: RenderOptions, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: RenderOptions, /) -> bool: ...

class ChannelDisplay(enum.Enum):
    """Channel display."""
    Color = 0

    Red = 1

    Green = 2

    Blue = 3

    Alpha = 4

def getChannelDisplayEnums() -> list[ChannelDisplay]:
    """Get every value of ChannelDisplay."""

class InputVideoLevels(enum.Enum):
    """Input video levels."""
    FromFile = 0

    FullRange = 1

    LegalRange = 2

def getInputVideoLevelsEnums() -> list[InputVideoLevels]:
    """Get every value of InputVideoLevels."""

class AlphaBlend(enum.Enum):
    """Alpha channel blending.

    References:
    - https://microsoft.github.io/Win2D/html/PremultipliedAlpha.htm
    """
    Straight = 1

    Premultiplied = 2

def getAlphaBlendEnums() -> list[AlphaBlend]:
    """Get every value of AlphaBlend."""

class ImageFilter(enum.Enum):
    """Image filtering."""
    Nearest = 0

    Linear = 1

    HighQuality = 2
    """A separable two pass resample with a wide kernel, rather than the four
    texels Linear reads. What it is for is minification: scaling an image down
    far enough that Linear misses most of it, which is what a thumbnail does
    and what the view does when it is zoomed out.
    """

def getImageFilterEnums() -> list[ImageFilter]:
    """Get every value of ImageFilter."""

class ImageFilters:
    """Image filters."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def minify(self) -> ImageFilter:
        """The filter for drawing an image smaller than it is."""

    @minify.setter
    def minify(self, arg: ImageFilter, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def magnify(self) -> ImageFilter:
        """The filter for drawing an image larger than it is."""

    @magnify.setter
    def magnify(self, arg: ImageFilter, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: ImageFilters, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: ImageFilters, /) -> bool: ...

class ImageOptions:
    """Image options."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def channelDisplay(self) -> ChannelDisplay:
        """Which channels are shown: the color, or one channel alone."""

    @channelDisplay.setter
    def channelDisplay(self, arg: ChannelDisplay, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def videoLevels(self) -> InputVideoLevels:
        """The video levels the image is taken to have. FromFile uses the
        image's own, ImageInfo::videoLevels.
        """

    @videoLevels.setter
    def videoLevels(self, arg: InputVideoLevels, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def alphaBlend(self) -> AlphaBlend:
        """How the image is blended with what is under it. None draws it
        opaque.
        """

    @alphaBlend.setter
    def alphaBlend(self, arg: AlphaBlend, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def imageFilters(self) -> ImageFilters:
        """The filters for drawing the image smaller or larger than it is."""

    @imageFilters.setter
    def imageFilters(self, arg: ImageFilters, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def cache(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the image's textures are kept in the texture cache, so that
        drawing the same image again does not copy it again. Off, they come
        from a pool shared by images of the same size and type, and the image
        is copied each time it is drawn unless reuse is on.
        """

    @cache.setter
    def cache(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: ImageOptions, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: ImageOptions, /) -> bool: ...

class ElideMode(enum.Enum):
    """Which end of an elided string to keep."""
    Right = 0
    """Keep the beginning: "ViewLayer.Combi...\""""

    Left = 1
    """Keep the end, for names that differ where they finish, such as a path or
    a layer: "...yer.Combined\"
    """

    Middle = 2
    """Keep both ends: "ViewLa...bined\""""

def elide(value: str, max: int = 32, mode: ElideMode = ElideMode.Right) -> str:
    """Elide a string to at most the given number of characters, not counting
    the ellipsis.
    """

    """Get filler text."""

@overload
def getLoremIpsum(lineCount: int) -> str:
    """Get filler text."""

    """Sleep for a given time."""

    """Sleep up to the given time."""

    """Convert a floating point rate to a rational."""

class Timer:
    """Timer."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context) -> None:
        """Create a new timer."""

    @property
    def repeating(self) -> bool:
        """Does the timer repeat?"""

    @repeating.setter
    def repeating(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    def start(self, arg0: float, arg1: Callable[[], None], /) -> None:
        """Start the timer."""

    def stop(self) -> None:
        """Stop the timer."""

    @property
    def active(self) -> bool:
        """Is the timer active?"""

    @property
    def timeout(self) -> datetime.timedelta:
        """Get the timeout."""

    """Initialize the library."""

    """Serialize a widget tree as JSON for inspection."""

    """
    Create a widget tree from JSON; returns the widget and a list of errors.
    """

def findWidget(widget: IWidget, id: str) -> IWidget:
    """Find a widget by the id it was given in the JSON."""

class TextureTypeObserver:
    """Value observer."""
    def __init__(self, observable: IObservableTextureType, callback: Callable[[TextureType], None], action: ObserverAction = ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

class IObservableTextureType:
    """Base class for observable values."""
    def get(self) -> TextureType:
        """Get the value."""

    def getObserversCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of observers."""

class ObservableTextureType(IObservableTextureType):
    """Observable value."""
    def __init__(self, arg: TextureType, /) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, arg: TextureType, /) -> None:
        """Set the value."""

    def setIfChanged(self, arg: TextureType, /) -> bool:
        """Set the value only if it has changed."""

    def get(self) -> TextureType:
        """Get the value."""

    """Child added event."""
    def __init__(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> None: ...

    @property

        """The child that was added, now the last of the parent's children."""

    @child.setter
    def child(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> None: ...

        """The child that was removed."""

    @property
    def index(self) -> int:
        """The index the child had among the parent's children."""

    @index.setter
    def index(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

class IDragDropData:
    """Base class for drag and drop data."""
    pass

class MouseEnterEvent:
    """Mouse enter event."""
    def __init__(self, arg: V2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def pos(self) -> V2I:
        """The cursor position, in pixels from the top left of the window: the
        coordinates widget geometry is in.
        """

    @pos.setter
    def pos(self, arg: V2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def accept(self) -> bool:
        """Set by the widget to take the hover: it is then sent the mouse
        moves, and a leave event when the cursor goes. Left unset, the widgets
        it is inside are asked in turn.
        """

    @accept.setter
    def accept(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

class MouseMoveEvent:
    """Mouse move event."""
    def __init__(self, arg0: V2I, arg1: V2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def pos(self) -> V2I:
        """The cursor position, in pixels from the top left of the window: the
        coordinates widget geometry is in.
        """

    @pos.setter
    def pos(self, arg: V2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def prev(self) -> V2I:
        """The cursor position before the move, in the same coordinates."""

    @prev.setter
    def prev(self, arg: V2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def accept(self) -> bool:
        """Set by a widget that handles the move. The window does not read it:
        a move goes to the pressed widget, or else to the hovered one, whatever
        this says.
        """

    @accept.setter
    def accept(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def dragDropData(self) -> IDragDropData:
        """Set by the pressed widget, as it is sent a move, to start a drag and
        drop of this data. The widget is then sent a release and a leave, and
        the widgets under the cursor are sent the drag events until the button
        is released.
        """

    @dragDropData.setter
    def dragDropData(self, arg: IDragDropData, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def dragDropCursor(self) -> Image:
        """An image drawn at the cursor while the drag and drop lasts, set with
        the data.
        """

    @dragDropCursor.setter
    def dragDropCursor(self, arg: Image, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def dragDropCursorHotspot(self) -> V2I:
        """The point in the cursor image that is put at the cursor, in pixels
        of the image.
        """

    @dragDropCursorHotspot.setter
    def dragDropCursorHotspot(self, arg: V2I, /) -> None: ...

    """Mouse buttons."""
    Left = 1

    Middle = 2

    Right = 3

    Extra1 = 4

    Extra2 = 5

def getMouseButtonEnums() -> list[MouseButton]:
    """Get every value of MouseButton."""

class KeyModifier(enum.Enum):
    """Keyboard modifiers.

    Note: This is a bitfield enum and is not compatible with FTK_ENUM, which
    requires a contiguous Count member. See to_string/from_string below for
    serialization support.
    """
    Shift = 1

    Control = 2

    Alt = 4

    Super = 8

commandKeyModifier: KeyModifier = KeyModifier.Super

def getKeyModifierLabel(arg: int, /) -> str:
    """Get a keyboard modifiers label."""

class MouseClickEvent:
    """Mouse click event."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg0: MouseButton, arg1: int, arg2: V2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def button(self) -> MouseButton:
        """The button pressed or released."""

    @button.setter
    def button(self, arg: MouseButton, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def modifiers(self) -> int:
        """The keyboard modifiers held, as KeyModifier flags."""

    @modifiers.setter
    def modifiers(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def pos(self) -> V2I:
        """The cursor position, in pixels from the top left of the window: the
        coordinates widget geometry is in.
        """

    @pos.setter
    def pos(self, arg: V2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def accept(self) -> bool:
        """Set by a widget to take the press: it becomes the pressed widget,
        which is sent the mouse moves and the release wherever the cursor goes.
        Left unset, the widgets under the cursor are asked in turn, deepest
        first, and if none takes it a right button can open a context menu. The
        release does not read it.
        """

    @accept.setter
    def accept(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def cancel(self) -> bool:
        """The press was taken away before it was released: a touch gesture
        started, or a finger rested long enough to be the right button
        (longPress). The release ends it without acting on it, so a button
        under the first finger does not click.
        """

    @cancel.setter
    def cancel(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

class ScrollEvent:
    """Scroll event (mouse wheel or touch pad)."""
    def __init__(self, arg0: V2F, arg1: int, arg2: V2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> V2F:
        """The amount scrolled, in mouse wheel steps rather than pixels: x
        across and y up and down.
        """

    @value.setter
    def value(self, arg: V2F, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def modifiers(self) -> int:
        """The keyboard modifiers held, as KeyModifier flags."""

    @modifiers.setter
    def modifiers(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def pos(self) -> V2I:
        """The cursor position, in pixels from the top left of the window: the
        coordinates widget geometry is in.
        """

    @pos.setter
    def pos(self, arg: V2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def accept(self) -> bool:
        """Set by a widget that takes the scroll. Left unset, the widgets under
        the cursor are asked in turn, deepest first, as far as a dialog.
        """

    @accept.setter
    def accept(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

class GestureEvent:
    """Touch gesture event: two fingers dragging and pinching."""
    def __init__(self, arg0: V2I, arg1: V2F, arg2: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def pos(self) -> V2I:
        """The point between the fingers."""

    @pos.setter
    def pos(self, arg: V2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def pan(self) -> V2F:
        """How far that point moved since the last event."""

    @pan.setter
    def pan(self, arg: V2F, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def zoom(self) -> float:
        """How much the distance between the fingers changed since the last
        event, as a ratio.
        """

    @zoom.setter
    def zoom(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def accept(self) -> bool:
        """Set by a widget to take the gesture as it starts: the rest of it
        goes to that widget, wherever the fingers go. Left unset, the widgets
        under the fingers are asked in turn, deepest first, as far as a dialog.
        """

    @accept.setter
    def accept(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

class KeyEvent:
    """Key event."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg0: Key, arg1: int, arg2: V2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def key(self) -> Key:
        """The key."""

    @key.setter
    def key(self, arg: Key, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def modifiers(self) -> int:
        """The keyboard modifiers held, as KeyModifier flags."""

    @modifiers.setter
    def modifiers(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def pos(self) -> V2I:
        """The cursor position, in pixels from the top left of the window: the
        coordinates widget geometry is in.
        """

    @pos.setter
    def pos(self, arg: V2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def accept(self) -> bool:
        """Set by a widget that takes the key: it is sent the release, and no
        other widget is asked. Left unset, the key focus widget and its parents
        are asked in turn, as far as a dialog, then the widgets under the
        cursor, deepest first; a Tab that none takes moves the key focus.
        """

    @accept.setter
    def accept(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

class TextEvent:
    """Text event."""
    def __init__(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def text(self) -> str:
        """The text entered, in UTF-8."""

    @text.setter
    def text(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def accept(self) -> bool:
        """Set by a widget that takes the text. The text goes to the key focus
        widget and, while this is unset, on to its parents in turn.
        """

    @accept.setter
    def accept(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

class DragDropTextData(IDragDropData):
    """Drag and drop text data."""
    def __init__(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def text(self) -> list[str]:
        """Get the text. For files dropped on the application from outside,
        their paths.
        """

class DragDropEvent:
    """Drag and drop event."""
    def __init__(self, arg0: V2I, arg1: V2I, arg2: IDragDropData, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def pos(self) -> V2I:
        """The cursor position, in pixels from the top left of the window: the
        coordinates widget geometry is in.
        """

    @pos.setter
    def pos(self, arg: V2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def prev(self) -> V2I:
        """The previous cursor position, in the same coordinates; for files
        dropped from outside the application, the same as pos.
        """

    @prev.setter
    def prev(self, arg: V2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def data(self) -> IDragDropData:
        """The data being dragged."""

    @data.setter
    def data(self, arg: IDragDropData, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def accept(self) -> bool:
        """Set by a widget, as it is sent the drag enter event, to be the drop
        target: it is then sent the drag moves, the drop and a leave. For files
        dropped from outside the application, set in the drop event to stop the
        widgets further out being asked.
        """

    @accept.setter
    def accept(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...
