class IWidget:
    """Base class for widgets."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, objectName: str, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @property
    def context(self) -> Context:
        """Get the context."""

    @property
    def objectName(self) -> str:
        """Get the object name. Widgets are given their class name when they
        are made, e.g. "ftk::PushButton".
        """

    @objectName.setter
    def objectName(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def objectPath(self) -> str:
        """Get the object path: the object names of the widget's parents and
        the widget, joined by "/".
        """

    @property
    def backgroundRole(self) -> ColorRole:
        """Get the background role."""

    @backgroundRole.setter
    def backgroundRole(self, arg: ColorRole, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def parent(self) -> IWidget:
        """Get the parent widget."""

    @parent.setter
    def parent(self, value: IWidget | None) -> None: ...

    def getChildren(self) -> list[IWidget]:
        """Get the children widgets."""

    def moveToFront(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> None:
        """Move the child widget to the front of the drawing order."""

    def moveToBack(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> None:
        """Move the child widget to the back of the drawing order."""

    @property
    def window(self) -> IWindow:
        """Get the window."""

    def getSizeHint(self) -> Size2I:
        """Get the size hint."""

    @property
    def hStretch(self) -> Stretch:
        """Get the horizontal layout stretch."""

    @hStretch.setter
    def hStretch(self, arg: Stretch, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def vStretch(self) -> Stretch:
        """Get the vertical layout stretch."""

    @vStretch.setter
    def vStretch(self, arg: Stretch, /) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def setStretch(self, horizontal: Stretch, vertical: Stretch) -> None:
        """Set the horizontal and vertical layout stretch."""

    @overload
    def setStretch(self, arg: Stretch, /) -> None:
        """Set the horizontal and vertical layout stretch."""

    @property
    def hAlign(self) -> HAlign:
        """Get the horizontal layout alignment."""

    @hAlign.setter
    def hAlign(self, arg: HAlign, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def vAlign(self) -> VAlign:
        """Get the vertical layout alignment."""

    @vAlign.setter
    def vAlign(self, arg: VAlign, /) -> None: ...

    def setAlign(self, horizontal: HAlign, vertical: VAlign) -> None:
        """Set the horizontal and vertical layout alignment."""

    def setGeometry(self, arg: Box2I, /) -> None:
        """Set the geometry. If this method is overridden the base method
        should be called.
        """

    @property
    def geometry(self) -> Box2I:
        """Get the geometry."""

    def setPos(self, arg: V2I, /) -> None:
        """Set the position."""

    def setSize(self, arg: Size2I, /) -> None:
        """Set the size."""

    def isVisible(self, andParentsVisible: bool = True) -> bool:
        """Is the widget visible?"""

    def setVisible(self, arg: bool, /) -> None:
        """Set whether the widget is visible. If this method is overridden the
        base method should be called.
        """

    def show(self) -> None:
        """Show the widget."""

    def hide(self) -> None:
        """Hide the widget."""

    @property
    def clipped(self) -> bool:
        """Is the widget clipped?"""

    @property
    def clipChildren(self) -> bool:
        """Does the widget clip its children?"""

    @clipChildren.setter
    def clipChildren(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def childrenClipRect(self) -> Box2I:
        """Get the clipping rect applied to the child widgets. By default this
        is the same as the widget geometry.
        """

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        """Is the widget enabled?"""

    @enabled.setter
    def enabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    def isEnabled(self, andParentsEnabled: bool = True) -> bool:
        """Is the widget enabled?"""

    @property
    def acceptsKeyFocus(self) -> bool:
        """Does this widget accept key focus?"""

    @acceptsKeyFocus.setter
    def acceptsKeyFocus(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    def moveToIndex(self, arg0: IWidget, arg1: int, /) -> None:
        """Move the child widget to the given index in the drawing order."""

    @property
    def keyFocus(self) -> bool:
        """Does this widget have key focus?"""

    def takeKeyFocus(self) -> None:
        """Take the key focus."""

    def releaseKeyFocus(self) -> None:
        """Release the key focus."""

    @property
    def tooltip(self) -> str:
        """Get the tooltip."""

    @tooltip.setter
    def tooltip(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    def setContextMenuCallback(self, arg: Callable[[], Menu], /) -> None:
        """Set the context menu callback. The callback is invoked when the
        widget is clicked with the right mouse button, and should return the
        menu to show, or null for no menu. Widgets without a callback pass the
        click to their parent.

        The click is offered to the widgets under the cursor first, so a widget
        that uses the right button for something else keeps it by accepting the
        press; only an unclaimed button opens a menu.

        The menu is created on demand rather than stored so that widgets only
        pay for it when it is used, and so that it can reflect the current
        state, for example disabling paste when the clipboard is empty.
        """

    def childAddEvent(self, event: ChildAddEvent) -> None:
        """Child add event."""

    def childRemoveEvent(self, event: ChildRemoveEvent) -> None:
        """Child remove event."""

    def tickEvent(self, parentsVisible: bool, parentsEnabled: bool, event: TickEvent) -> None:
        """Tick event. If this method is overridden the base method should be
        called.
        """

    def styleEvent(self, event: StyleEvent) -> None:
        """Style event."""

    def sizeHintEvent(self, event: SizeHintEvent) -> None:
        """Size hint event."""

    def clipEvent(self, clipRect: Box2I, clipped: bool) -> None:
        """Clip event. If this method is overridden the base method should be
        called.
        """

    def drawEvent(self, drawRect: Box2I, event: DrawEvent) -> None:
        """Draw event. This runs before the children are drawn, so anything
        drawn here is behind them; use drawOverlayEvent() to draw over them.
        """

    def drawOverlayEvent(self, drawRect: Box2I, event: DrawEvent) -> None:
        """Draw overlay event. This runs after the children are drawn, which is
        where a border or a highlight belongs when the children fill the
        widget.
        """

    def mouseEnterEvent(self, arg: MouseEnterEvent, /) -> None:
        """Mouse enter event."""

    def mouseLeaveEvent(self) -> None:
        """Mouse leave event."""

    def mouseMoveEvent(self, event: MouseMoveEvent) -> None:
        """Mouse move event."""

    def mousePressEvent(self, event: MouseClickEvent) -> None:
        """Mouse press event."""

    def mouseReleaseEvent(self, event: MouseClickEvent) -> None:
        """Mouse release event."""

    def scrollEvent(self, event: ScrollEvent) -> None:
        """Scroll event."""

    def gestureEvent(self, event: GestureEvent) -> None:
        """Touch gesture event. The widget that accepts the first event of a
        gesture receives the rest of it.
        """

    def keyFocusEvent(self, focus: bool) -> None:
        """Key focus event. If this method is overridden the base method should
        be called.
        """

    def keyPressEvent(self, event: KeyEvent) -> None:
        """Key press event."""

    def keyReleaseEvent(self, event: KeyEvent) -> None:
        """Key release event."""

    def textEvent(self, event: TextEvent) -> None:
        """Text event."""

    def setSizeUpdate(self, value: bool = True) -> None:
        """Set a size update. The sizeHintEvent() and setGeometry() methods
        will be called the next tick of the event loop.
        """

    def setDrawUpdate(self, value: bool = True) -> None:
        """Set a draw update. The drawEvent() method will be called the next
        tick of the event loop.
        """

    def dragEnterEvent(self, event: DragDropEvent) -> None:
        """Drag enter event."""

    def dragLeaveEvent(self, event: DragDropEvent) -> None:
        """Drag leave event."""

    def dragMoveEvent(self, event: DragDropEvent) -> None:
        """Drag move event."""

    def dropEvent(self, event: DragDropEvent) -> None:
        """Drop event."""

class IContainer(IWidget):
    """Base class for widgets that are one child filling them.

    Most composite widgets are a layout, or a scroll area, or a tab widget,
    given the whole of the parent. Written by hand that is the same two methods
    every time:


    Size2I X::getSizeHint() const { return _layout->getSizeHint(); } void
    X::setGeometry(const Box2I& v) {
        IWidget::setGeometry(v);
        _layout->setGeometry(v);
    }


    Deriving from this and calling _setWidget() instead says the same thing
    once. Widgets that lay their children out themselves derive from IWidget as
    before; this is only for the ones that hand everything to one child.
    """
    def __init__(self, context: Context, objectName: str, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @property
    def widget(self) -> IWidget:
        """Get the child filling this widget."""

class WindowBufferType(enum.Enum):
    """Window offscreen buffer types."""
    U8 = 0

    F16 = 1

    F32 = 2

class WindowBufferTypeObserver:
    """Value observer."""
    def __init__(self, observable: IObservableWindowBufferType, callback: Callable[[WindowBufferType], None], action: ObserverAction = ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

class IObservableWindowBufferType:
    """Base class for observable values."""
    def get(self) -> WindowBufferType:
        """Get the value."""

    def getObserversCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of observers."""

class ObservableWindowBufferType(IObservableWindowBufferType):
    """Observable value."""
    def __init__(self, arg: WindowBufferType, /) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, arg: WindowBufferType, /) -> None:
        """Set the value."""

    def setIfChanged(self, arg: WindowBufferType, /) -> bool:
        """Set the value only if it has changed."""

    def get(self) -> WindowBufferType:
        """Get the value."""

class IWindow(IWidget):
    """Base class for windows."""
    @property
    def app(self) -> App:
        """Get the application."""

    @property
    def windowID(self) -> int:
        """Get the window ID."""

    @property
    def screen(self) -> int:
        """Get which screen the window is on."""

    @property
    def title(self) -> str:
        """Get the window title."""

    @title.setter
    def title(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def size(self) -> Size2I:
        """Get the window size, in the units the window system sizes windows
        in, which are not pixels everywhere; see getPixelDensity().
        """

    @size.setter
    def size(self, arg: Size2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def minSize(self) -> Size2I:
        """Get the minimum window size, in the same units."""

    @minSize.setter
    def minSize(self, arg: Size2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def fullScreen(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the window has been set to full screen with
        setFullScreen().
        """

    @fullScreen.setter
    def fullScreen(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeFullScreen(self) -> IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether the window has been set to full screen."""

    @property
    def floatOnTop(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the window is set to float on top of the other windows.
        """

    @floatOnTop.setter
    def floatOnTop(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeFloatOnTop(self) -> IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether the window floats on top."""

    def getWindowInfo(self) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
        """Get the window information."""

    @property
    def bufferSize(self) -> Size2I:
        """Get the size of the window's buffer, in pixels: what the widgets are
        laid out and drawn in.
        """

    @property
    def bufferType(self) -> WindowBufferType:
        """Get the type of the offscreen buffer the window is drawn into."""

    @bufferType.setter
    def bufferType(self, arg: WindowBufferType, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeBufferType(self) -> IObservableWindowBufferType:
        """Observe the offscreen buffer type."""

    @property
    def contentScale(self) -> float:
        """Get the ratio of the buffer size to the window size, or zero before
        the window has a size.
        """

    @property
    def displayScale(self) -> float:
        """Get the display scale the window's widgets are sized and drawn at.
        The application sets it; see App::getWindowDisplayScale().
        """

    @displayScale.setter
    def displayScale(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeDisplayScale(self) -> IObservableFloat:
        """Observe the display scale."""

    @property
    def keyFocus(self) -> IWidget:
        """Get the widget with the key focus, or null for none."""

    @keyFocus.setter
    def keyFocus(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> None: ...

    def getNextKeyFocus(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> IWidget:
        """Get the widget after the given one in the order Tab moves the key
        focus in: the enabled widgets that accept the focus, in the window's
        last child, the one on top. It wraps around, gives the first widget for
        one not in the order, and null when the order is empty.
        """

    def getPrevKeyFocus(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> IWidget:
        """Get the widget before the given one in the key focus order; see
        getNextKeyFocus(). It gives the last widget for one not in the order.
        """

    @property
    def tooltipsEnabled(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether tooltips are shown in the window."""

    @tooltipsEnabled.setter
    def tooltipsEnabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def cursorPos(self) -> V2I:
        """Get the cursor position."""

    @property
    def dragDropActive(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether a drag and drop is in progress. Drag events only reach
        the widget under the cursor, so a widget that reacts to a drag being
        anywhere near it -- a scroll area moving a drop target into reach --
        asks here.
        """

    def layout(self, size: Size2I) -> None:
        """Lay the window out at a size, as a resize from the window system
        would.

        Until this happens the window and everything in it has an empty
        geometry, and nothing is under the cursor -- so a test that reads a
        geometry, or aims at one, is reading and aiming at nothing. It does not
        fail; it passes, having checked nothing.
        """

    def click(self, pos: V2I, button: MouseButton = MouseButton.Left, modifiers: int = 0) -> None:
        """Move the cursor there, then press and release a mouse button."""

    def drag(self, path: Sequence[V2I], modifiers: int = 0, release: bool = True, holdModifiers: int = 0) -> None:
        """Press at the first point, move through the rest, release.

        Moved in steps between the points rather than jumped, because a widget
        that treats a drag as one gesture and a widget that treats every move
        as a separate edit look identical from a single move -- and the
        difference between them is the whole question for undo. Points beyond
        the second are how a drag that goes somewhere and comes back is
        written.
        """

    def setTouchInput(self, value: bool) -> None:
        """Make the mouse events that follow a finger's, or a mouse's again,
        for the widgets that treat a fingertip differently.
        """

    def cancelPress(self) -> None:
        """Let go of what press() holds, cancelled rather than released, the
        way a second finger landing takes a press away.
        """

    def keyPress(self, key: Key, modifiers: int = 0) -> None:
        """Press a key and release it."""

    def text(self, text: str) -> None:
        """Enter text, the way typing does after the key events: letters reach
        a widget as text input, not as key presses.
        """

    def textEditing(self, text: str, cursor: int = 0) -> None:
        """Send an input method composition, the way an IME does while text is
        being composed; committing is text().
        """

    def setIcon(self, arg: Image, /) -> None:
        """Set the window icon.

        Icon images should be of type ImageType::RGBA_U8, with no mirroring,
        memory alignment of one, and LSB memory endian.

        Window icons are not supported on macOS.
        """

    def screenshot(self, arg: Box2I, /) -> Image:
        """Capture a screenshot."""

    def close(self) -> None:
        """Close the window."""

    def setCloseCallback(self, arg: Callable[[], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the window close callback."""

    def setFullScreenCallback(self, arg: Callable[[bool], None], /) -> None:
        """Set a function called once the window has entered or left full
        screen. On macOS the change animates, and setFullScreen() is only its
        start: what is drawn during the animation is a snapshot of the window
        stretched to the screen.
        """

class IMouseWidget(IWidget):
    """Base class for widgets with simple mouse interactions."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, objectName: str, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

class IPopup(IWidget):
    """Base class for popups."""
    def close(self) -> None:
        """Close the popup."""

class DialogSize(enum.Enum):
    """How a dialog is sized in the window it opens in. Never larger than the
    window, whichever it is.
    """
    Fit = 0
    """As big as its content asks for, or across the window in a direction the
    content's stretch expands in. For messages, questions and settings.
    """

    Text = 1
    """A column of text: as wide as the text width, or as the content if that
    is wider, and the height of the window. For agreements, notes and help,
    which are read rather than glanced at, and whose lines are hard to follow
    when they run across a wide window.
    """

    Full = 2
    """The window, less the dialog margin. For lists and reports, which use
    whatever room there is.
    """

def getDialogSizeEnums() -> list[DialogSize]:
    """Get every value of DialogSize."""

class IDialog(IPopup):
    """Base class for dialog widgets."""
    def open(self, arg: IWindow, /) -> None:
        """Open the dialog.

        Should setVisible() be used instead of open() and close()?
        """

    def isOpen(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the dialog is open."""

    def setCloseCallback(self, arg: Callable[[], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the close callback."""

    @property
    def dialogSize(self) -> DialogSize:
        """Get how the dialog is sized."""

    @property
    def textWidth(self) -> int:
        """Get the width of a DialogSize::Text dialog, in characters."""

    def setDialogSize(self, size: DialogSize, textWidth: int = 100) -> None:
        """Set how the dialog is sized, and for DialogSize::Text, how many
        characters wide it is, measured as a label's wrap width is. Fit, the
        default, is what the content's stretch says. Text and Full decide the
        size themselves, whatever the content's stretch, so their content
        should fill the room it is given: labels in it wrapping to fit, a
        scroll widget expanding.
        """

    """Menu popup type."""
    Menu = 0

    SubMenu = 1

        Open the popup at a position, for example at the cursor for a context
        menu.
        """

    @overload
    def open(self, window: IWindow, pos: V2I) -> None:
        """Open the popup.

        Should setVisible() be used instead of open() and close()?

        Open the popup at a position, for example at the cursor for a context
        menu.
        """

    def isOpen(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the popup is open."""

    def setCloseCallback(self, callback: Callable[[], None]) -> None:

    def setPopup(self, type: MenuPopup) -> None:

        """Get whether the window is maximized."""

    def maximized(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def normalGeometry(self) -> Box2I:
        """Get the position and size the window has when it is neither
        maximized nor full screen: what to remember it by.
        """

class ActionCheckType(enum.Enum):
    """How an action carries a checked state."""
    Check = 1
    """A switch. Picking it turns something on or off."""

    Radio = 2
    """One of several. Picking it selects; picking the one already selected
    leaves it selected, because there is no such thing as none of them.

    Set by ActionGroup rather than by hand: an action is one of many only in
    the company of the others.
    """

class ActionCheckTypeObserver:
    """Value observer."""
    def __init__(self, observable: IObservableActionCheckType, callback: Callable[[ActionCheckType], None], action: ObserverAction = ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

class IObservableActionCheckType:
    """Base class for observable values."""
    def get(self) -> ActionCheckType:
        """Get the value."""

    def getObserversCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of observers."""

class ObservableActionCheckType(IObservableActionCheckType):
    """Observable value."""
    def __init__(self, arg: ActionCheckType, /) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, arg: ActionCheckType, /) -> None:
        """Set the value."""

    def setIfChanged(self, arg: ActionCheckType, /) -> bool:
        """Set the value only if it has changed."""

    def get(self) -> ActionCheckType:
        """Get the value."""

class KeyShortcut:
    """Keyboard shortcut."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, key: Key, modifier: KeyModifier) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, key: Key, modifier: KeyModifier, modifier2: KeyModifier) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, key: Key, modifier: KeyModifier, modifier2: KeyModifier, modifier3: KeyModifier) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, key: Key, modifiers: int = 0) -> None: ...

    @property
    def key(self) -> Key:
        """The key, or Unknown for none."""

    @key.setter
    def key(self, arg: Key, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def modifiers(self) -> int:
        """The keyboard modifiers held, as KeyModifier flags."""

    @modifiers.setter
    def modifiers(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

class Action:
    """Action."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self, text: str, callback: Callable[[], None]) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, text: str, icon: str, callback: Callable[[], None]) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, text: str, shortcut: KeyShortcut, callback: Callable[[], None]) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, text: str, icon: str, shortcut: KeyShortcut, callback: Callable[[], None]) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, text: str, checkedCallback: Callable[[bool], None]) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, text: str, icon: str, checkedCallback: Callable[[bool], None]) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, text: str, shortcut: KeyShortcut, checkedCallback: Callable[[bool], None]) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, text: str, icon: str, shortcut: KeyShortcut, checkedCallback: Callable[[bool], None]) -> None: ...

    @property
    def text(self) -> str:
        """Get the text, shown in menus and on buttons."""

    @text.setter
    def text(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeText(self) -> IObservableString:
        """Observe the text."""

    @property
    def icon(self) -> str:
        """Get the name of the icon; empty for none."""

    @icon.setter
    def icon(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeIcon(self) -> IObservableString:
        """Observe the icon."""

    @property
    def checkedIcon(self) -> str:
        """Get the name of the icon shown while the action is checked; empty to
        show the other icon.
        """

    @checkedIcon.setter
    def checkedIcon(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeCheckedIcon(self) -> IObservableString:
        """Observe the checked icon."""

    @property
    def shortcuts(self) -> list[KeyShortcut]:
        """Get the keyboard shortcuts. An action made without one has a single
        shortcut with no key.
        """

    @shortcuts.setter
    def shortcuts(self, arg: Sequence[KeyShortcut], /) -> None: ...

    def doCallback(self) -> None:
        """Call the callback, if the action has one. Menus and tool buttons
        call it when the action is picked, checkable or not.
        """

    @property
    def checkType(self) -> ActionCheckType:
        """Get how the action carries a checked state: Check when it was made
        with a checked callback, None otherwise. An ActionGroup sets it for the
        actions added to it.
        """

    @checkType.setter
    def checkType(self, arg: ActionCheckType, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def checkable(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the action carries a checked state at all."""

    @property
    def checked(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the action is checked."""

    @checked.setter
    def checked(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeCheckType(self) -> IObservableActionCheckType:
        """Observe the check type."""

    @property
    def observeChecked(self) -> IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether the action is checked."""

    def doCheckedCallback(self, arg: bool, /) -> None:
        """Call the checked callback with the given state, if the action has
        one. The checked state is not changed; see setChecked().
        """

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the action is enabled. The menus and buttons showing it
        follow it, and the shortcut of a disabled action does nothing.
        """

    @enabled.setter
    def enabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeEnabled(self) -> IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether the action is enabled."""

    @property
    def tooltip(self) -> str:
        """Get the tooltip."""

    @tooltip.setter
    def tooltip(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeTooltip(self) -> IObservableString:
        """Observe the tooltip."""

class ActionGroupType(enum.Enum):
    """Action group type."""
    Click = 0

    Check = 1

    Radio = 2

    Toggle = 3

def getActionGroupTypeEnums() -> list[ActionGroupType]:
    """Get every value of ActionGroupType."""

class ActionGroup:
    """A group of related actions.

    ButtonGroup does this for widgets, and cannot be used for actions: a menu
    makes its own buttons, so the application never sees them, and one action
    commonly drives several -- the same action is a menu item and a tool bar
    button at once. Relatedness belongs where identity is, which is the action
    rather than the widget.

    Radio is the case worth having. Without it an application writes, for every
    set of mutually exclusive actions, an observer that walks the set calling
    setChecked(this one == the current one), and creates the actions with a
    plain callback so that picking one cannot un-pick it. That works and is not
    discoverable from anything.
    """
    def __init__(self, type: ActionGroupType) -> None:
        """Create a new group."""

    @property
    def actions(self) -> list[Action]:
        """Get the actions."""

    def addAction(self, arg: Action, /) -> None:
        """Add an action. The group sets its check type."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Remove every action, leaving them as they are."""

    @property
    def checked(self) -> int:
        """Get the index of the checked action, or -1 for none. Only a radio
        group keeps it as the actions are picked.
        """

    @checked.setter
    def checked(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    def observeChecked(self) -> IObservableInt:
        """Observe the index of the checked action."""

    def setCheckedCallback(self, arg: Callable[[int, bool], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the callback. The index is which action, the bool its new state;
        for a radio group the bool is always true, since picking one is the
        only thing that can happen.
        """

class ColorStyle(enum.Enum):
    """Color style."""
    Dark = 0

    Light = 1

def getColorStyleEnums() -> list[ColorStyle]:
    """Get every value of ColorStyle."""

class Renderer(enum.Enum):
    """What an application's windows are drawn with."""
    OpenGL = 0

    GPU = 1
    """The GPU renderer, Metal or Vulkan, where it is built and a device can be
    made for it, and OpenGL otherwise.
    """

def getRendererEnums() -> list[Renderer]:
    """Get every value of Renderer."""

class ColorControls:
    """Color controls."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def brightness(self) -> float:
        """The brightness the color roles are given, as a multiplier; one
        leaves them as they are.
        """

    @brightness.setter
    def brightness(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def contrast(self) -> float:
        """The contrast the color roles are given; one leaves them as they are.
        """

    @contrast.setter
    def contrast(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def disabledAlpha(self) -> float:
        """Alpha multiplier applied by getColorRole(ColorRole, bool enabled)
        when a widget is disabled. Since widgets are alpha-composited, this
        dims toward the underlying surface.
        """

    @disabledAlpha.setter
    def disabledAlpha(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: ColorControls, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: ColorControls, /) -> bool: ...

class Style:
    """Style."""
    @property
    def colorControls(self) -> ColorControls:
        """Get the color controls: the brightness and contrast of the color
        roles, and the alpha of disabled widgets.
        """

    @colorControls.setter
    def colorControls(self, arg: ColorControls, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def fonts(self) -> dict[FontType, str]:
        """Get the font names, by font type."""

    @fonts.setter
    def fonts(self, arg: Mapping[FontType, str], /) -> None: ...

    def getSizeRole(self, role: SizeRole, scale: float) -> int:
        """Get a size role in pixels at the given display scale; zero for a
        role the style has no size for.
        """

    def getColorRole(self, role: ColorRole) -> Color4F:
        """Get a color role for a widget state. When enabled is false the
        color's alpha is multiplied by ColorControls::disabledAlpha, dimming it
        toward the surface it is drawn over.
        """

class ColorStyleObserver:
    """Value observer."""
    def __init__(self, observable: IObservableColorStyle, callback: Callable[[ColorStyle], None], action: ObserverAction = ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

class IObservableColorStyle:
    """Base class for observable values."""
    def get(self) -> ColorStyle:
        """Get the value."""

    def getObserversCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of observers."""

class ObservableColorStyle(IObservableColorStyle):
    """Observable value."""
    def __init__(self, arg: ColorStyle, /) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, arg: ColorStyle, /) -> None:
        """Set the value."""

    def setIfChanged(self, arg: ColorStyle, /) -> bool:
        """Set the value only if it has changed."""

    def get(self) -> ColorStyle:
        """Get the value."""

class MonitorInfo:
    """Monitor information."""
    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """The monitor's name."""

    @name.setter
    def name(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def size(self) -> Size2I:
        """The size of the monitor's current display mode."""

    @size.setter
    def size(self, arg: Size2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def refreshRate(self) -> int:
        """The refresh rate of the current display mode, in hertz; zero where
        it is not known.
        """

    @refreshRate.setter
    def refreshRate(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def dpi(self) -> V2F:
        """The horizontal and vertical dots per inch. Not set in SDL3 builds,
        where it is zero.
        """

    @dpi.setter
    def dpi(self, arg: V2F, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def bounds(self) -> Box2I:
        """The monitor's area of the desktop, in screen coordinates."""

    @bounds.setter
    def bounds(self, arg: Box2I, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: MonitorInfo, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: MonitorInfo, /) -> bool: ...

class MonitorInfoListObserver:
    """List observer."""
    def __init__(self, observableList: IObservableMonitorInfoList, callback: Callable[[Sequence[MonitorInfo]], None], action: ObserverAction = ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

class IObservableMonitorInfoList:
    """Base class for observable lists."""
    pass

class ObservableMonitorInfoList(IObservableMonitorInfoList):
    """Observable list."""
    def __init__(self, arg: Sequence[MonitorInfo], /) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, arg: Sequence[MonitorInfo], /) -> None:
        """Set the list."""

    def setIfChanged(self, arg: Sequence[MonitorInfo], /) -> bool:
        """Set the list only if it has changed."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear the list."""

    def setItem(self, index: int, value: MonitorInfo) -> None:
        """Set an item."""

    def setItemOnlyIfChanged(self, index: int, value: MonitorInfo) -> bool:
        """Set an item only if it has changed."""

    @overload
    def pushBack(self, arg: MonitorInfo, /) -> None:
        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

    @overload
    def pushBack(self, arg: Sequence[MonitorInfo], /) -> None:
        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

    def insertItem(self, index: int, value: MonitorInfo) -> None:
        """Insert an item."""

    def insertItems(self, index: int, list: Sequence[MonitorInfo]) -> None:
        """Insert a range of items."""

    def removeItem(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Remove an item."""

    def removeItems(self, start: int, end: int) -> None:
        """Remove a range of items."""

    def replaceItems(self, start: int, end: int, list: Sequence[MonitorInfo]) -> None:
        """Replace a range of items."""

    def get(self) -> list[MonitorInfo]:
        """Get the list."""

    def getSize(self) -> int:
        """Get the list size."""

    def isEmpty(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the list is empty."""

    def getItem(self, arg: int, /) -> MonitorInfo:
        """Get a list item."""

    def contains(self, arg: MonitorInfo, /) -> bool:
        """Does the list contain the given item?"""

    def indexOf(self, arg: MonitorInfo, /) -> int:
        """Get the index of the given item."""

class AppFiles:
    """Where an application keeps its per-user files: the settings and the log.
    Left empty, no files are kept and the application is responsible for its
    own.

    A suite of applications gives them all the same directory and tells them
    apart by the base name, so that one directory holds the settings and logs
    of all of them rather than one directory apiece.
    """
    def __init__(self, dirName: str = '', baseName: str = '', version: int = 0) -> None: ...

    @property
    def dirName(self) -> str:
        """Directory under the user's documents. Empty keeps no files."""

    @dirName.setter
    def dirName(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def baseName(self) -> str:
        """Base name for the settings and log files. Empty uses the application
        name.
        """

    @baseName.setter
    def baseName(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def version(self) -> int:
        """Appended to the base name when greater than zero, so that two major
        versions of an application do not read each other's settings.
        """

    @version.setter
    def version(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

class App(IApp):
    """Base class for user interface applications."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, argv: Sequence[str], name: str, summary: str, cmdLineArgs: Sequence[ICmdLineArg] = [], cmdLineOptions: Sequence[ICmdLineOption] = [], appFiles: AppFiles = ...) -> None: ...

    @property
    def settings(self) -> Settings:
        """Get the settings. Null when no AppFiles was given."""

    @property
    def settingsPath(self) -> pathlib.Path:
        """Get the settings file path. Empty when no AppFiles was given."""

    @property
    def logFilePath(self) -> pathlib.Path:
        """Get the log file path. Empty when no AppFiles was given."""

    @property
    def windows(self) -> list[IWindow]:
        """Get the windows."""

    @property
    def observeMonitors(self) -> IObservableMonitorInfoList:
        """Observe the monitors."""

    @property
    def fontSystem(self) -> FontSystem:
        """Get the font system."""

    @property
    def iconSystem(self) -> IconSystem:
        """Get the icon system."""

    @property
    def style(self) -> Style:
        """Get the style."""

    @property
    def colorStyle(self) -> ColorStyle:
        """Get the color style. Dark unless the -colorStyle command line option
        or setColorStyle() says otherwise.
        """

    @colorStyle.setter
    def colorStyle(self, arg: ColorStyle, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def renderer(self) -> Renderer:
        """Get the renderer that is set, which is OpenGL unless the other is
        asked for. What draws is said by gpu::isEnabled(): this is what is kept
        with the settings, and where the GPU renderer cannot draw OpenGL does
        whatever was asked.
        """

    @renderer.setter
    def renderer(self, arg: Renderer, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeRenderer(self) -> "ftk::IObservable<ftk::Renderer>":
        """Observe the renderer that is set."""

    @property
    def observeColorStyle(self) -> IObservableColorStyle:
        """Observe the color style."""

    @property
    def defaultDisplayScale(self) -> float:
        """Get the display scale found at startup: the first display's, or the
        -displayScale command line option's, and never less than one.
        """

    @property
    def autoDisplayScale(self) -> float:
        """Get the display scale that setDisplayScale(0) gives: the window's
        once there is one, else the display's.
        """

    @property
    def displayScale(self) -> float:
        """Get the display scale. A window on a display of another scale can
        draw at that one instead; see getWindowDisplayScale().
        """

    @displayScale.setter
    def displayScale(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeDisplayScale(self) -> IObservableFloat:
        """Observe the display scale."""

    @property
    def tooltipsEnabled(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether tooltips are shown. On by default, for every window."""

    @tooltipsEnabled.setter
    def tooltipsEnabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeTooltipsEnabled(self) -> IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether tooltips are shown."""

    @staticmethod
    def setOffscreenDefault(value: bool) -> None:
        """Set whether applications start offscreen, before any of them exist.

        For test runners and batch tools. An application that is not there to
        be looked at should not be putting windows over whatever the person at
        the keyboard is doing -- and a window that can be clicked while
        something drives it is a run that can be interfered with, which is
        worse than untidy.

        Static because the decision belongs to whoever started the process
        rather than to any one application in it, and a test suite makes
        dozens.
        """

    def writeScreenshot(self, path: str | os.PathLike) -> bool:
        """Write a screenshot of the first window. Returns false when there is
        no window, when the offscreen buffer is not ready, or when the file
        cannot be written; the reason is logged.

        Only useful once the event loop has run: that is what realizes and
        sizes the window and leaves a buffer behind to read.
        """

    def writeWidgetDump(self, path: str | os.PathLike) -> bool:
        """Write the first window's widget tree as JSON; see widgetDump().
        Returns false when there is no window or the file cannot be written;
        the reason is logged. Only useful once the event loop has run and laid
        the window out.
        """

    def exit(self) -> None:
        """Exit the application."""

    def run(self) -> None:
        """Run the application."""

    def tick(self) -> None:
        """Tick the event loop. If this method is overridden the base method
        should be called.
        """

class ComboBox(IWidget):
    """Combo box."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: Context, items: Sequence[ComboBoxItem], parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: Context, items: Sequence[str], parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    def getItems(self) -> list[ComboBoxItem]:
        """Get the items."""

    @overload
    def setItems(self, arg: Sequence[ComboBoxItem], /) -> None:
        """Set the items."""

    @overload
    def setItems(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None:
        """Set the items."""

    @property
    def currentIndex(self) -> int:
        """Get the current index."""

    @currentIndex.setter
    def currentIndex(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    def setElide(self, max: int, mode: ElideMode = ElideMode.Right) -> None:
        """Set the number of characters shown when the box is closed, and which
        end of a longer item to keep. Zero, the default, shows the whole of the
        longest item, which is what makes the box as wide as its longest item
        however short the current one is. The menu is never elided, so the
        whole of each item can still be read when choosing.
        """

    def setIndexCallback(self, arg: Callable[[int], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the current index callback."""

    def setItemCallback(self, arg: Callable[[ComboBoxItem], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the current item callback."""

    @property
    def font(self) -> FontType:
        """Get the font."""

    @font.setter
    def font(self, arg: FontType, /) -> None: ...

class ConfirmDialog(IDialog):
    """Confirmation dialog."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, title: str, text: str, confirm: str = 'OK', cancel: str = 'Cancel', parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

    def setCallback(self, arg: Callable[[bool], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the callback."""

class ChoiceDialog(IDialog):
    """Choice dialog: a question answered by one of several buttons, e.g. save,
    discard, or cancel. The last choice is the safe one -- it takes the key
    focus, so the key that takes the dialog at face value is the one that
    changes nothing.
    """
    def __init__(self, context: Context, title: str, text: str, choices: Sequence[str], parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

    def setCallback(self, arg: Callable[[int], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the callback. It is given the index of the chosen button;
        dismissing the dialog chooses nothing and the callback does not run.
        """

class InputDialog(IDialog):
    """Text input dialog."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, title: str, text: str, value: str, confirm: str = 'OK', cancel: str = 'Cancel', parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

    def setCallback(self, arg: Callable[[str], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the callback. It is called once, when the input is accepted with
        the confirm button or the Return key; cancelling closes the dialog
        without calling it.
        """

class ItemButton(IButton):
    """A button that draws the list item states around a widget, for list rows
    built from more than a line of text.
    """
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

    @property
    def widget(self) -> IWidget:
        """Get the widget."""

    @widget.setter
    def widget(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> None: ...

    def setFocusCallback(self, arg: Callable[[bool], None], /) -> None:
        """Set a callback for when the item gains or loses the key focus."""

    def setDragDropDataCallback(self, arg: Callable[[], IDragDropData], /) -> None:
        """Set the drag and drop data the item offers. Setting it makes the
        item draggable: a press that moves past the drag length starts a drag
        instead of a click.
        """

    def setDragDropCursorCallback(self, arg: Callable[[], Image], /) -> None:
        """Set the image shown under the cursor while the item is dragged."""

class ItemControls(IMouseWidget):
    """A group of controls inside an item row: the mouse stops here, so the
    gaps between the controls go quiet instead of hovering the item underneath,
    and a click that misses a control does nothing rather than acting as a
    click on the item.
    """
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

    @property
    def widget(self) -> IWidget:
        """Get the widget."""

    @widget.setter
    def widget(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> None: ...

class DiagWidget(IContainer):
    """Diagnostics widget."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

    @property
    def marginRole(self) -> SizeRole:
        """Get the margin role."""

    @marginRole.setter
    def marginRole(self, arg: SizeRole, /) -> None: ...

class DialogSystem(ISystem):
    """Dialog system."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context) -> None:
        """Create a new system."""

    def message(self, title: str, text: str, window: IWindow) -> MessageDialog:
        """Open a message dialog."""

    def choice(self, title: str, text: str, choices: Sequence[str], window: IWindow, callback: Callable[[int], None]) -> ChoiceDialog:
        """Open a choice dialog. The callback is given the index of the chosen
        button; dismissing the dialog chooses nothing.
        """

    def input(self, title: str, text: str, value: str, window: IWindow, callback: Callable[[str], None]) -> InputDialog:
        """Open a text input dialog. The callback is called when the input is
        accepted; cancelling closes the dialog without it.
        """

    def confirm(self, title: str, text: str, window: IWindow, callback: Callable[[bool], None], confirm: str = 'OK', cancel: str = 'Cancel') -> ConfirmDialog:
        """Open a confirmation dialog."""

class Divider(IWidget):
    """Divider widget."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, orientation: Orientation, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

def updateDividers(parent: IWidget) -> None:
    """Show each divider among a widget's children only between visible
    children, and one between any two: a divider beside a group that is hidden
    would stand at the end of the row, or next to another. Call it when the
    children's visibility changes.
    """

class IDocument:
    """Base class for documents."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

class IDocumentObserver:
    """Value observer."""
    def __init__(self, observable: IObservableIDocument, callback: Callable[[IDocument], None], action: ObserverAction = ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

class IObservableIDocument:
    """Base class for observable values."""
    def get(self) -> IDocument:
        """Get the value."""

    def getObserversCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of observers."""

class ObservableIDocument(IObservableIDocument):
    """Observable value."""
    def __init__(self, value: IDocument | None) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, value: IDocument | None) -> None:
        """Set the value."""

    def setIfChanged(self, value: IDocument | None) -> bool:
        """Set the value only if it has changed."""

    def get(self) -> IDocument:
        """Get the value."""

class IObservableWeakIDocument:
    """Base class for observable values."""
    def get(self) -> IDocument | None:
        """Get the value."""

    def getObserversCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of observers."""

class WeakIDocumentObserver:
    """Value observer."""
    def __init__(self, observable: IObservableWeakIDocument, callback: Callable[[IDocument | None], None], action: ObserverAction = ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

class IDocumentListObserver:
    """List observer."""
    def __init__(self, observableList: IObservableIDocumentList, callback: Callable[[Sequence[IDocument]], None], action: ObserverAction = ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

class IObservableIDocumentList:
    """Base class for observable lists."""
    pass

class ObservableIDocumentList(IObservableIDocumentList):
    """Observable list."""
    def __init__(self, arg: Sequence[IDocument], /) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, arg: Sequence[IDocument], /) -> None:
        """Set the list."""

    def setIfChanged(self, arg: Sequence[IDocument], /) -> bool:
        """Set the list only if it has changed."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear the list."""

    def setItem(self, index: int, value: IDocument) -> None:
        """Set an item."""

    def setItemOnlyIfChanged(self, index: int, value: IDocument) -> bool:
        """Set an item only if it has changed."""

    @overload
    def pushBack(self, arg: IDocument, /) -> None:
        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

    @overload
    def pushBack(self, arg: Sequence[IDocument], /) -> None:
        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

    def insertItem(self, index: int, value: IDocument) -> None:
        """Insert an item."""

    def insertItems(self, index: int, list: Sequence[IDocument]) -> None:
        """Insert a range of items."""

    def removeItem(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Remove an item."""

    def removeItems(self, start: int, end: int) -> None:
        """Remove a range of items."""

    def replaceItems(self, start: int, end: int, list: Sequence[IDocument]) -> None:
        """Replace a range of items."""

    def get(self) -> list[IDocument]:
        """Get the list."""

    def getSize(self) -> int:
        """Get the list size."""

    def isEmpty(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the list is empty."""

    def getItem(self, arg: int, /) -> IDocument:
        """Get a list item."""

    def contains(self, arg: IDocument, /) -> bool:
        """Does the list contain the given item?"""

    def indexOf(self, arg: IDocument, /) -> int:
        """Get the index of the given item."""

class DocumentModel:
    """Document model."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context) -> None:
        """Create a new document model."""

    def getList(self) -> list[IDocument]:
        """Get the documents."""

    def observeList(self) -> IObservableIDocumentList:
        """Observe the documents."""

    def add(self, document: IDocument) -> None:
        """Add a document. It becomes the current document."""

    def observeAdd(self) -> IObservableWeakIDocument:
        """Observe the documents as they are added."""

    def close(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Close the document at the given index; an index out of range is
        ignored. Closing the current document makes the next one current, or
        the last one when it was the last.
        """

    def closeAll(self) -> None:
        """Close all of the documents. This sends observeCloseAll(), not
        observeClose() for each.
        """

    def observeClose(self) -> IObservableWeakIDocument:
        """Observe the documents as close() closes them: each one is sent
        before it is removed.
        """

    def observeCloseAll(self) -> IObservableBool:
        """Observe closeAll(): true is sent each time it is called."""

    def getCurrent(self) -> IDocument:
        """Get the current document, or null for none."""

    @property
    def currentIndex(self) -> int:
        """Get the index of the current document, or -1 for none. An index set
        is clamped to the documents.
        """

    @currentIndex.setter
    def currentIndex(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    def observeCurrent(self) -> IObservableIDocument:
        """Observe the current document."""

    def observeCurrentIndex(self) -> IObservableInt:
        """Observe the index of the current document."""

class DoubleModel:
    """Double precision floating point value model."""
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Create a new model."""

    @property
    def value(self) -> float:
        """Get the value, which is kept within the range."""

    @value.setter
    def value(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def setValueSoft(self, arg: float, /) -> None:
        """Set the value, extending a soft range to admit it. This is for
        values the user typed; interactive changes such as dragging use
        setValue(), which always clamps, so they cannot run the range away.
        """

    def observeValue(self) -> IObservableDouble:
        """Observe the value."""

    @property
    def range(self) -> RangeD:
        """Get the range the value is kept within. The default is 0 to 1."""

    @range.setter
    def range(self, arg: RangeD, /) -> None: ...

    def observeRange(self) -> IObservableRangeD:
        """Observe the range."""

    @property
    def rangeSoft(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the range is soft. A value given to setValueSoft()
        beyond a soft range extends the range instead of being clamped.
        """

    @rangeSoft.setter
    def rangeSoft(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def step(self) -> float:
        """Get the step, the amount a step increments or decrements the value
        by. The default is 0.1.
        """

    @step.setter
    def step(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def largeStep(self) -> float:
        """Get the large step, the amount a large step increments or decrements
        the value by. The default is 1.
        """

    @largeStep.setter
    def largeStep(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def stepInc(self) -> None:
        """Increment the value by a step."""

    def stepDec(self) -> None:
        """Decrement the value by a step."""

    def largeStepInc(self) -> None:
        """Increment the value by a large step."""

    def largeStepDec(self) -> None:
        """Decrement the value by a large step."""

    @property
    def hasDefault(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether there is a default value."""

    def observeHasDefault(self) -> IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether there is a default value."""

    @property
    def defaultValue(self) -> float:
        """Get the default value."""

    @defaultValue.setter
    def defaultValue(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def observeDefault(self) -> IObservableDouble:
        """Observe the default value."""

    def setDefault(self) -> None:
        """Set the default value.

        Set the value to the default value.
        """

    def clearDefault(self) -> None:
        """Clear the default value."""

class DoubleEdit(IContainer):
    """Double precision floating point value editor."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: Context, model: DoubleModel, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> float:
        """Get the value, which is kept within the range."""

    @value.setter
    def value(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def setCallback(self, arg: Callable[[float], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the callback, called with the value whenever it changes,
        including from setValue() and from other widgets that share the model.
        Typed text is applied when Enter is pressed or the key focus is lost.
        """

    @property
    def range(self) -> RangeD:
        """Get the range the value is kept within."""

    @range.setter
    def range(self, arg: RangeD, /) -> None: ...

    def setRange(self, arg0: float, arg1: float, /) -> None:
        """Set the range. The value is clamped to the new range.

        Set the range from its minimum and maximum.
        """

    @property
    def step(self) -> float:
        """Get the step: how much the up and down arrow keys, the increment
        buttons, and the scroll wheel change the value by.
        """

    @step.setter
    def step(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def largeStep(self) -> float:
        """Get the large step: how much Page Up and Page Down, and the scroll
        wheel with Shift held, change the value by.
        """

    @largeStep.setter
    def largeStep(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def defaultValue(self) -> float:
        """Get the default value."""

    @defaultValue.setter
    def defaultValue(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def getModel(self) -> DoubleModel:
        """Get the model."""

    @property
    def precision(self) -> int:
        """Get the display precision."""

    @precision.setter
    def precision(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def font(self) -> FontType:
        """Get the font, the monospace font by default."""

    @font.setter
    def font(self, arg: FontType, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def borderRole(self) -> ColorRole:
        """Get the border role."""

    @borderRole.setter
    def borderRole(self, arg: ColorRole, /) -> None: ...

class FileBrowserOpenOptions:
    """File browser open options."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def title(self) -> str:
        """The title of the browser."""

    @title.setter
    def title(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def path(self) -> pathlib.Path:
        """The directory to open at. Empty stays wherever the browser was last
        left.
        """

    @path.setter
    def path(self, arg: str | os.PathLike, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def mode(self) -> FileBrowserMode:
        """Whether a file is opened or saved, or a directory chosen."""

    @mode.setter
    def mode(self, arg: FileBrowserMode, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def fileName(self) -> str:
        """A suggested file name for saving."""

    @fileName.setter
    def fileName(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def extensions(self) -> list[str]:
        """Restrict the listing to these extensions, e.g. { ".djvr" }. Empty
        shows every file.
        """

    @extensions.setter
    def extensions(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def extensionsLabel(self) -> str:
        """Names the group of extensions: the filter group in the native
        dialog, and the entry shown in place of "*.*" in the built-in one.
        """

    @extensionsLabel.setter
    def extensionsLabel(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def multiple(self) -> bool:
        """Allow more than one file to be chosen. Only meaningful when opening;
        there is one file to save to and one directory to pick.
        """

    @multiple.setter
    def multiple(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    def removeItem(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Remove an item."""

    def removeItems(self, start: int, end: int) -> None:
        """Remove a range of items."""

    def replaceItems(self, start: int, end: int, list: Sequence[FileBrowserExtGroup]) -> None:
        """Replace a range of items."""

    def get(self) -> list[FileBrowserExtGroup]:
        """Get the list."""

    def getSize(self) -> int:
        """Get the list size."""

    def isEmpty(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the list is empty."""

    def getItem(self, arg: int, /) -> FileBrowserExtGroup:
        """Get a list item."""

    def contains(self, arg: FileBrowserExtGroup, /) -> bool:
        """Does the list contain the given item?"""

    def indexOf(self, arg: FileBrowserExtGroup, /) -> int:
        """Get the index of the given item."""

class FileBrowserModel:
    """File browser model: the current path and its history, the options and
    the extensions.
    """
    def __init__(self, context: Context) -> None:
        """Create a new model."""

    @property
    def path(self) -> pathlib.Path:
        """Get the current path."""

    @path.setter
    def path(self, arg: str | os.PathLike, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observePath(self) -> IObservableFileSystemPath:
        """Observe the current path."""

    def forward(self) -> None:
        """Go forward to the next path."""

    @property
    def observeHasForward(self) -> IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether there is a next path."""

    def back(self) -> None:
        """Go back to the previous path."""

    @property
    def observeHasBack(self) -> IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether there is a previous path."""

    @property
    def options(self) -> FileBrowserOptions:
        """Get the options."""

    @options.setter
    def options(self, arg: FileBrowserOptions, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeOptions(self) -> IObservableFileBrowserOptions:
        """Observe the options."""

    @property
    def exts(self) -> list[str]:
        """Get the extensions."""

    @exts.setter
    def exts(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeExts(self) -> IObservableStringList:
        """Observe the extensions."""

    @property
    def ext(self) -> str:
        """Get the current extension."""

    @ext.setter
    def ext(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeExt(self) -> IObservableString:
        """Observe the current extension."""

    @property
    def extGroups(self) -> list[FileBrowserExtGroup]:
        """Get the extension groups."""

    @extGroups.setter
    def extGroups(self, arg: Sequence[FileBrowserExtGroup], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeExtGroups(self) -> IObservableFileBrowserExtGroupList:
        """Observe the extension groups."""

    @property
    def extGroup(self) -> str:
        """Get the current extension group, by label; empty for none."""

    @extGroup.setter
    def extGroup(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeExtGroup(self) -> IObservableString:
        """Observe the current extension group."""

class FileBrowserSystem(ISystem):
    """File browser system."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context) -> None:
        """Create a new system."""

    def open(self, window: IWindow, callback: Callable[[Path], None], options: FileBrowserOpenOptions = ...) -> None:
        """Open the file browser.

        Open the file browser for more than one file. Set
        FileBrowserOpenOptions::multiple for the choosing to allow it; without
        that this reports the one file chosen.
        """

    def openMultiple(self, window: IWindow, callback: Callable[[Sequence[Path]], None], options: FileBrowserOpenOptions = ...) -> None: ...

    @property
    def nativeFileDialog(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the native file dialog is used."""

    @nativeFileDialog.setter
    def nativeFileDialog(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def model(self) -> FileBrowserModel:
        """Get the file browser model."""

    @property
    def recentDirsModel(self) -> RecentFilesModel:
        """Get the recent directories model.

        What the browser's recent list shows. The directory of every choice
        made in the browser is added to it, whatever the choice was for -- a
        LUT's as well as a movie's -- and it is a list of its own, apart from
        an application's recent files, so those choices do not join them. An
        application that opens files some other way, from the command line or
        by drag and drop, adds their directories here itself if the browser is
        to offer them.
        """

    @recentDirsModel.setter
    def recentDirsModel(self, arg: RecentFilesModel, /) -> None: ...

def to_json(arg: FileBrowserOptions, /) -> str:
    """Serialize a path.

    The frames a path covers are its own state rather than part of its name, so
    a path written as its name alone comes back naming one file. This writes
    them beside it, as data: a sequence has a run for each hole in it, with a
    step as well as a range, and a name made to carry all of that would have to
    be parsed back out again.

    A path whose name already says what it covers -- a single file, or one
    frame -- is written as that name, so the ordinary case reads and writes as
    it always did.
    """

def from_json(arg0: str, arg1: FileBrowserOptions, /) -> None:
    """Convert from JSON, given as a string, into the given value."""

class FileBrowserView(IWidget):
    """File browser view widget."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, mode: FileBrowserMode, model: FileBrowserModel, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

    def reload(self) -> None:
        """Reload the directory."""

    def setCallback(self, arg: Callable[[Sequence[Path]], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the callback. Carries everything selected, so that opening one
        of several chosen files opens the ones chosen.
        """

    def hasPaths(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether a list of files is shown in place of a directory."""

    def getPaths(self) -> list[Path]:
        """Get the list of files shown in place of a directory."""

    def setPaths(self, paths: Sequence[Path]) -> None:
        """Show a list of files in place of the model's directory: recent
        files, say. They are shown in the order given, each with the directory
        it is in, and the search filter matches against the whole path. The
        extensions chosen in the model do not apply. A directory in the list,
        which is a path ending in a separator, is given to the callback like a
        file. The file system is not asked about the files, so their sizes are
        not shown.
        """

    def clearPaths(self) -> None:
        """Go back to showing the model's directory."""

    def setCurrent(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Set the current item, which selects it: for moving into the list
        from a search box, say.
        """

    def setSelectCallback(self, arg: Callable[[Sequence[Path]], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the selection callback. More than one path only when selecting
        more than one is allowed; empty when nothing is selected.
        """

    @property
    def multiple(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether more than one file can be selected."""

    @multiple.setter
    def multiple(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def selection(self) -> list[Path]:
        """Get the selection."""

    @property
    def search(self) -> str:
        """Get the search filter."""

    @search.setter
    def search(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeCurrent(self) -> IObservableInt:
        """Observe the current item."""

    def getRect(self, arg: int, /) -> Box2I:
        """Get the rectangle of an item."""

class FloatModel:
    """Floating point value model."""
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Create a new model."""

    @property
    def value(self) -> float:
        """Get the value, which is kept within the range."""

    @value.setter
    def value(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def setValueSoft(self, arg: float, /) -> None:
        """Set the value, extending a soft range to admit it. This is for
        values the user typed; interactive changes such as dragging use
        setValue(), which always clamps, so they cannot run the range away.
        """

    def observeValue(self) -> IObservableFloat:
        """Observe the value."""

    @property
    def range(self) -> RangeF:
        """Get the range the value is kept within. The default is 0 to 1."""

    @range.setter
    def range(self, arg: RangeF, /) -> None: ...

    def observeRange(self) -> IObservableRangeF:
        """Observe the range."""

    @property
    def rangeSoft(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the range is soft. A value given to setValueSoft()
        beyond a soft range extends the range instead of being clamped.
        """

    @rangeSoft.setter
    def rangeSoft(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def step(self) -> float:
        """Get the step, the amount a step increments or decrements the value
        by. The default is 0.1.
        """

    @step.setter
    def step(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def largeStep(self) -> float:
        """Get the large step, the amount a large step increments or decrements
        the value by. The default is 1.
        """

    @largeStep.setter
    def largeStep(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def stepInc(self) -> None:
        """Increment the value by a step."""

    def stepDec(self) -> None:
        """Decrement the value by a step."""

    def largeStepInc(self) -> None:
        """Increment the value by a large step."""

    def largeStepDec(self) -> None:
        """Decrement the value by a large step."""

    @property
    def hasDefault(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether there is a default value."""

    def observeHasDefault(self) -> IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether there is a default value."""

    @property
    def defaultValue(self) -> float:
        """Get the default value."""

    @defaultValue.setter
    def defaultValue(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def observeDefault(self) -> IObservableFloat:
        """Observe the default value."""

    def setDefault(self) -> None:
        """Set the default value.

        Set the value to the default value.
        """

    def clearDefault(self) -> None:
        """Clear the default value."""

class FloatEdit(IContainer):
    """Floating point value editor."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: Context, model: FloatModel, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> float:
        """Get the value, which is kept within the range."""

    @value.setter
    def value(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def setCallback(self, arg: Callable[[float], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the callback, called with the value whenever it changes,
        including from setValue() and from other widgets that share the model.
        Typed text is applied when Enter is pressed or the key focus is lost.
        """

    @property
    def range(self) -> RangeF:
        """Get the range the value is kept within."""

    @range.setter
    def range(self, arg: RangeF, /) -> None: ...

    def setRange(self, arg0: float, arg1: float, /) -> None:
        """Set the range. The value is clamped to the new range.

        Set the range from its minimum and maximum.
        """

    @property
    def step(self) -> float:
        """Get the step: how much the up and down arrow keys, the increment
        buttons, and the scroll wheel change the value by.
        """

    @step.setter
    def step(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def largeStep(self) -> float:
        """Get the large step: how much Page Up and Page Down, and the scroll
        wheel with Shift held, change the value by.
        """

    @largeStep.setter
    def largeStep(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def defaultValue(self) -> float:
        """Get the default value."""

    @defaultValue.setter
    def defaultValue(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def getModel(self) -> FloatModel:
        """Get the model."""

    @property
    def precision(self) -> int:
        """Get the display precision."""

    @precision.setter
    def precision(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def font(self) -> FontType:
        """Get the font, the monospace font by default."""

    @font.setter
    def font(self, arg: FontType, /) -> None: ...

class FlowLayout(IWidget):
    """Flow layout.

    Children are placed left to right and wrap onto a new line when the next
    one will not fit. Use this where a horizontal layout would be right if only
    it always had the room -- a legend, a row of tags, a toolbar in a panel the
    user can make narrow.

    The height depends on the width, which the size hint has no way to ask
    about, so the layout reports the tallest single child until it has been
    given a geometry, then reports what that width actually needed. Laying one
    out therefore settles over two passes rather than one.
    """
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new layout."""

    @property
    def marginRole(self) -> SizeRole:
        """Get the margin role."""

    @marginRole.setter
    def marginRole(self, arg: SizeRole, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def spacingRole(self) -> SizeRole:
        """Get the spacing role."""

    @spacingRole.setter
    def spacingRole(self, arg: SizeRole, /) -> None: ...

class FormGroup:
    """A group of form layouts whose labels share one column width, so that
    forms in separate sections of a panel line up as one would.

    The width is that of the widest visible label in any of the forms, and is
    known when the first of them is sized: a form asks the group, which
    measures the labels of all of them. A form whose section is closed still
    counts, so opening a section does not move the others.
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Create a new group."""

def setFormGroup(widget: IWidget, group: FormGroup | None) -> None:
    """Put every form layout among a widget and its descendants into a group:
    for a panel assembled from widgets that each hold a form of their own.
    Forms added to them afterwards are not included.
    """

class FormLayout(IContainer):
    """Form layout."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new layout."""

    def addRow(self, text: str, widget: IWidget) -> int:
        """Add a row."""

    @overload
    def removeRow(self, arg: int, /) -> None:
        """Remove a row."""

    @overload
    def removeRow(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> None:
        """Remove a row."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear all of the rows."""

    @overload
    def setRowVisible(self, arg0: int, arg1: bool, /) -> None:
        """Set row visibility."""

    @overload
    def setRowVisible(self, arg0: IWidget, arg1: bool, /) -> None:
        """Set row visibility."""

    @property
    def marginRole(self) -> SizeRole:
        """Get the margin role."""

    @marginRole.setter
    def marginRole(self, arg: SizeRole, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def spacingRole(self) -> SizeRole:
        """Get the spacing role."""

    @spacingRole.setter
    def spacingRole(self, arg: SizeRole, /) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def addSpacer(self) -> int:
        """Add a spacer."""

    @overload
    def addSpacer(self, arg: SizeRole, /) -> int:
        """Add a spacer."""

    @property
    def group(self) -> FormGroup:
        """Get the group the layout's labels share their width with."""

    @group.setter
    def group(self, value: FormGroup | None) -> None: ...

class GraphLabel:
    """One line on a graph: its color, the format string for its readout, and
    how the sample is turned into the number that format expects.
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def colorRole(self) -> ColorRole:
        """The color role the line is drawn in. It also names the line to
        setSamples() and addSample().
        """

    @colorRole.setter
    def colorRole(self, arg: ColorRole, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def text(self) -> str:
        """The format string for the line's readout, with {0} for the latest
        sample.
        """

    @text.setter
    def text(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def format(self) -> DiagFormat:
        """How the sample is turned into the number the readout shows."""

    @format.setter
    def format(self, arg: DiagFormat, /) -> None: ...

class GraphWidget(IContainer):
    """Graph widget."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, title: str, labels: Sequence[GraphLabel], parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

    def setSamples(self, arg0: ColorRole, arg1: Sequence[int], /) -> None:
        """Set the samples."""

    def addSample(self, arg0: ColorRole, arg1: int, /) -> None:
        """Add a sample."""

class GridLayout(IWidget):
    """Grid layout."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new layout."""

    def getGridPos(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> tuple[int, int]:
        """Get the grid position of the given child."""
